entries.subject: Inbox: show MMS photos at a usable size and make video playable
entries.title: Inbox: show MMS photos at a usable size and make video playable
entries.body:
Kevin's four photos rendered as 110px slivers stacked down one side of an
otherwise empty bubble, and the video showed as the word "attachment" with no
player and no way to save it - which is most of the reason the message still
looked like nothing had arrived.

Photos now sit in a wrapping row, bounded at 300x420 rather than 220x240, and
click through to full size. Video gets a real player. Every attachment, any
type, has a download link, and /api/inbox/media/:id/:idx takes ?download=1 so
the browser saves the file instead of streaming it.

Both the Inbox thread and the compact conversation view share one Attachments
component, so they cannot drift apart again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Recover inbound MMS that fell between the two text webhooks
entries.title: Recover inbound MMS that fell between the two text webhooks
entries.body:
Kevin Lamparek sent two media-only MMS to the Hub number on 2026-10-30 at
13:26 and 13:31 CT. Neither was stored, and nothing was logged.

/twilio-inbound skipped them: isGroupParticipant() is true for his number
because he sits on a group conversation, so the 1:1 handler defers to
/conversations-webhook. That webhook never fired - the MMS never entered the
Conversations service at all, which Twilio's own conversation message list
confirms (it still ends at 13:19). The message fell through the gap between
the two handlers with no row and no notification.

Twilio retains the media, so this adds the three reads needed to get it back:

  GET  /api/admin/twilio-media?phone=   messages carrying media, with sids and
                                        whether the Hub already holds each one
  GET  /api/admin/twilio-media/file     streams one media item, so the bytes can
                                        be fetched without the Twilio credentials
                                        leaving the server
  POST /api/admin/twilio-media/recover  writes the missing inbound rows, keyed on
                                        the external_id the webhook would have
                                        used, so it is idempotent and a later fix
                                        to the webhooks cannot duplicate them.
                                        ?dry=1 previews. Sends nothing.

Recovery only. The webhook gap itself is untouched here and still needs fixing -
any message from a group participant that does not route through Conversations
is dropped the same way, plain text included.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Stop the Sierra sync stripping address-audit and bare FB Ad tags
entries.title: Stop the Sierra sync stripping address-audit and bare FB Ad tags
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-29, after reading the tag durability audit: deal with the
wider exposure, not just the home value tag.

Two of the three exposed writers are closed here because their tags have
a recognisable shape. The third - arbitrary tags from Automations and the
bulk-tag button - cannot be pattern-matched and needs tag-origin
tracking, which is a schema change and a separate decision.

ADDRESS AUDIT TAGS. 491 were applied on 2026-10-29. Sierra never sees
them and nothing re-applies them, so each one was due to go on its
lead's next sync pass. Nothing has been lost yet - all 221 this session
wrote were re-read and still present - but every one of those leads has
been reported by Sierra at least once in the past year, 8 of them within
the last month, so the whole set would have drained within a year.

BARE 'FB Ad'. ai.js builds 'FB Ad' + (property ? ': ' + property : ''),
and the whitelist was /^FB Ad:/ with the colon, so a lead with no
property name was unprotected. Two clients today. Pre-existing.

ON REMOVAL, because the predicate is easy to read backwards: it preserves
a tag that is ON THE HUB RECORD, it does not resurrect one. Remove the
tag in the Hub and it stays removed - the Hub is master. What it stops is
a Sierra-side removal silently deleting Hub-owned information.

Why the large tag counts are not evidence against any of this: Import
sits on 42,984 clients and Realist on 15,600 because SIERRA supplies them
on every pass. They never needed protecting. Only Hub-invented tags are
exposed, which is the whole set this predicate now names.

Tests pin both directions - every Hub-written shape survives, and
'FB Adjacent', 'Address' and the Sierra-supplied tags are not force-kept.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home value: tag the source, and stop the sync stripping the tag
entries.title: Home value: tag the source, and stop the sync stripping the tag
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-29: "make sure we get a tagging for those who request their
home value on the NEW link." Two separate problems sat behind that, and
the first was a silent failure rather than a missing feature.

THE TAG WAS BEING STRIPPED. Tags are Sierra-owned in sierra-helper.js:
a sync pass replaces them and only a short whitelist of Hub-native tags
is unioned back in. The home value tag was not on that list, so every
sync pass removed it. James Osullivan was tagged by the intake at 20:35
on 2026-10-27 and the 22:02 sync took it off; the three submissions from
the new /home-value/ page came back from Sierra with tags=[] for the same
reason. A home value requester therefore looked like any other lead in
both systems, which is what John was asking about.

The Home Value Requested smart list kept working throughout only because
it ORs in the home_value_submission activity row. The tag half of that
condition has been unreliable for as long as the whitelist has existed.

WHICH DOOR, TAGGED SEPARATELY. The canonical tag cannot answer it: its
name is the retired seller site and it is deliberately left that way,
because the smart list matches it and renaming it would orphan every
historic requester. So a new-link submission now also carries
"Home Value: mattsmithteam.com/home-value", keyed on the HV_Source line
the form writes - never on the page URL, which says /contact/ for every
submission because the form posts through a hidden iframe there and
Sierra overwrites Sent_From from its own page context.

Both tag shapes are now Hub-native, so neither survives at Sierra's
pleasure. The trade-off is the same one FB Ad tags already accept:
deleting one in Sierra no longer sticks, because the Hub re-adds it.

Tests: 189 pass across the home-value and AI-guard suites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Fix bulk-tags corrupting the JSON-array tags field
entries.title: bulk-tags corrupting the JSON-array tags field
entries.body:
A naive split(',') on an existing JSON-array tags string shredded it
into bracket/quote fragments and re-glued the new tag outside the
array (e.g. ["a","b"], New Tag instead of ["a","b","New Tag"]),
breaking any later JSON.parse(tags) caller. Read with parseTags()
and always write back valid JSON.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home value: repoint the tool, fire the intake, and guard the AI away
entries.title: Home value: repoint the tool, fire the intake, and guard the AI away
entries.body:
The home value tool moved off the Sierra seller site onto the native
questionnaire at mattsmithteam.com/home-value. Three things had to change
Hub-side, and the first two were silent failures rather than cosmetic.

THE LINK. VALUE_TOOL_URL is the one place 73 templates resolve through
({{home_value_url}}, {{home_value_link}}, {{cma_request_link}}), so the
move is a single line. Only template 384 hard-coded its CTA, at
/sellers/home-value/, which was already returning 404 - that one was
fixed in the live Hub rather than here.

THE INTAKE. Both doors gated on the OLD notification subject, so a
submission titled "Home Value Request" matched neither and no follow-up
email was sent - and because enrollHvSms and scheduleConditionQuestion
both sit inside `if (emailed?.ok)`, no email meant no sequence at all.
The native form also shares NO field names with the seller site: it posts
through Sierra's /contact/ form, so identity is First_Name / Last_Name /
Email / Phone, not *Name* / *Email Address*. Parsed against the wrong
scheme the email address comes out empty and the submission is skipped
without a trace, which is what /sellers/free-market-analysis/ has always
done. Labels are now read with the asterisk wrapper optional, because
notifications use *Label*: value and the stored Sierra note uses Label:.

HV_Submission_ID replaces the submitted-at timestamp as the dedupe key
where present. Sierra merges on email, so a homeowner asking again months
later was previously indistinguishable from their first submission and
would have been swallowed as "already processed". The old key is still
checked so nothing already handled re-sends.

THE AI GUARD. server/ai-followup/ did not mention home_value_sms
anywhere, so nothing stopped the AI texting or answering a value
requester - and since earning a reply is the entire point of that
sequence, the reply path is what would have fired. Matt's rule is that no
AI follow-up touches anyone who asks what their home is worth, and the
note's "DO NOT ENROL" line is a label, not a guard. Same three layers
FSBO and Cancelled/Expired got on 2026-10-05:

  ai-enrollment.js  never picked up in the first place
  forbidden.js      refused wherever a message would leave, every path
  orchestrator.js   refused on reply, above the force gate

Each asks about the SUBMISSION as well as the campaign row, because that
row only exists once the day-0 email succeeded - a requester whose email
bounced would otherwise carry no guard at all.

Format spec: Home Value Site/home-value-form/SUBMISSION-FORMAT.md
Tests: 185 pass across the home-value and AI-guard suites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: The home value list on the Dashboard, and a cache bump so it is seen
entries.title: The home value list on the Dashboard, and a cache bump so it is seen
entries.body:
THE LIST. The tile gave a count; this says WHO. A "Home Value Requests" section
under Cancelled/Expired/FSBO Updates, newest request first, because the one that
came in this morning is the one worth acting on. A repeat requester carries a
"3x" badge - asking twice is a stronger signal than asking once - and each row
opens the client. Counts and rows come from the same SMART_LIST_SQL as the
Clients smart list, so the three views cannot disagree.

EXCLUDING BY HAND. The marker moves from `Not a Lead` to `HV: Exclude - <reason>`.
The generic phrase was wrong the first time it met a real case: Kim Vipond is a
PAST CLIENT who sold with another agent - not a lead to drop everywhere, just not
a home value prospect - and a generic marker would have followed her into every
list written later. Now scoped to this list alone.

THE CACHE. CACHE_NAME had not moved since 2026-09-30, and the old cache is only
purged when it changes, so every frontend deploy in between shipped chunks that
returning tabs never saw. That is why the tile "wasn't there" - it was, in a
fresh tab. Bumped to v10.

Its own test pinned the literal 'mst-hub-v9', so it failed on exactly the change
it exists to encourage and passed for the thirteen months the name never moved.
It now asserts the shape, which is all the file can prove.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: A home value request types the lead seller, and shows on the Dashboard
entries.title: A home value request types the lead seller, and shows on the Dashboard
entries.body:
Two things John asked for on 2026-10-28.

TYPE. A lead created BY the intake was always typed seller; an existing one kept
whatever it arrived as. That is how ten homeowners ended up on the Home Value
list typed `buyer` - mostly Realist imports, where the type records where the
record came from rather than what the person wants. Asking what your own house
is worth is seller intent, so a `buyer` is switched on submission and the change
is written to activity_log so it shows on the timeline.

Only `buyer` is switched. `both` already carries seller and flipping it would
throw the buyer half away; `seller` is already right and writes nothing.

This is not cosmetic: `type` drives campaign routing and the FUB stage mapping,
where prime + buyer lands a seller lead in High Probability BUYERS.

DASHBOARD. A "Home Value Requests" tile in the action-card row, deep-linking to
/clients?smart=home_value_requested (the Clients page already reads ?smart=).
The count comes from the same SMART_LIST_SQL the list uses, so the tile and the
rows behind it cannot disagree.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Keep the team's own records off the Home Value list
entries.title: Keep the team's own records off the Home Value list
entries.body:
John test-submitted the home value form on 2026-10-08 and turned up on his own
lead list. Deleting the submission row would have been the quick fix, but it is
true history, and testing the form is a thing that will keep happening.

So the record keeps its log and a tag keeps it off lead lists:
`Internal - Not a Lead`. Matched on the ASCII phrase "Not a Lead" so no dash
character has to survive a round trip through the API and SQLite. Tag any other
staff or test record the same way and it drops off without a code change.

Covered both ways: a tagged record with a real submission is excluded, and an
ordinary lead whose tags merely mention leads ("Lead Ad", "Buyer Lead") is not.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: A smart list for everyone who asked what their home is worth
entries.title: A smart list for everyone who asked what their home is worth
entries.body:
Clients > Smart Lists > "Home Value · Requested". Dead and Do Not Contact are
excluded, as asked.

Two sources OR'd, because neither alone is the whole set: the
'home_value_submission' row the intake writes to activity_log, which is the
authoritative record and reaches back furthest, and the site tag it adds at the
same moment, kept because a lead can carry that tag from a Sierra sync without
the intake ever having run. On 2026-10-28 only 20 leads carried the tag, so the
tag alone would have been a short list. A repeat requester appears once.

Deliberately NOT the WORKABLE predicate: that also drops hub_text_opt_out, and
someone who stopped our texts still asked what their house is worth and still
belongs here - the home value campaign is email.

Also adds an index on activity_log(entity_type, entity_id, action). The list
asks the log per client, and the smart-lists endpoint counts every list on each
Clients page load; unindexed that is a scan of the whole log for every one of
46k clients - the same shape that cost 6.99s of an 8.0s load before
marion_condo_viewers was precomputed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Junk outranks a stale MLS tag, so a closed lead is not reopened
entries.title: Junk outranks a stale MLS tag, so a closed lead is not reopened
entries.body:
stageFor() checked mls_status FIRST and returned immediately, so a junk lead
whose mls_status still said "expired" was pushed to FUB's Expired stage - a
WORKABLE stage. Eric Londquist (#29745) went Dead -> Expired on today's run.

He is junk precisely BECAUSE his house went back on the market, which makes the
MLS tag the out-of-date fact and the junk the current one (John, 2026-10-27).

The expired/cancelled rule exists for leads sitting in `watch`, where sending
'Watch' would throw away what the Hub knows. It was never meant to reopen a lead
a person had deliberately closed - that same rule already says junk is a human's
call and must never be touched (enforceWatchForMlsTagged, 2026-09-18, and
expired-watch-rule.test.mjs).

Watch and new leads keep the specific Expired/Cancelled stage exactly as before;
only junk and donotcontact now win over it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Let a FUB status push be scoped to the statuses you meant
entries.title: Let a FUB status push be scoped to the statuses you meant
entries.body:
A dry run over all 3,317 candidates showed what an unscoped sweep would do: 156
junk/DNC changes, which is what was asked for, and 163 others that were not.

Most of those 163 move leads OUT of "High Probability Sellers" INTO "High
Probability Buyer", decided by the Hub's `type` field - the same field we found
wrong on 52 Realist homeowners that day. They were seller leads typed buyer
because a Realist import said so. Pushing that would have overwritten real FUB
segmentation from data we already knew was unreliable.

candidates(), remaining() and pushStatuses() take onlyStatuses; the endpoint
takes `statuses: ["junk","donotcontact"]`. Omitting it keeps the old behaviour,
and an empty array falls back to the full sweep rather than silently selecting
nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Answer a home value request on the next minute, not the next ten
entries.title: Answer a home value request on the next minute, not the next ten
entries.body:
James Osullivan submitted a Seller CMA Request at 20:25:47 on 2026-10-27 and
was answered at 20:35:08. Nothing was broken; we were not looking yet.

- The 60-second inbox poll already opens the connection and parses every new
  message, so it now recognises the notification and runs the intake on that
  pass, the same way FUB lead emails are already intercepted. The 10-minute
  All Mail sweep stays as the backstop, because a Gmail filter that skips the
  inbox would make the interception blind - exactly how the FUB notifications
  were missed on 2026-09-17.
- Deduping moves to the submitted-at string inside the email body, which is
  identical whichever door sees it first. Arrival time is not: two doors
  seconds apart either side of a minute boundary would have emailed the
  person twice. The old key is still checked so nothing already processed
  re-fires.
- The client timeline returned {"error":"no such column: status"} for EVERY
  client in the Hub. transactions uses property_status/property_address, and
  showings has no status column at all; one bad column inside a single
  try/catch took every other section down with it. This is why a request
  could be recorded correctly and still look like it never arrived.
- A canceled or failed condition question no longer blocks the real one
  forever. "One per person, ever" now means one they actually received or one
  still on its way.
- A different phone number on the form is kept as an alt instead of being
  discarded. He submitted (319) 321-0659 while the Hub held (319) 431-4988
  from a Realist import; the known number still wins, but both survive.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: One owner per lead, one gate before every automated text
entries.title: One owner per lead, one gate before every automated text
entries.body:
Eight paths could text a buyer and routing was decided once, at enrolment.
Nothing re-asked at send time whether another lane had taken the lead over, so
on 2026-10-26 a Willowridge ad lead had a cold-buyer message and a listing
opener queued for the same 3:15 PM from two different records.

- preSendGate() is now the single question asked before any automated
  prospecting text. It reuses canAutomatedSend and adds ownership plus a
  weekly prospecting budget counted across every campaign. The AI lane used
  to skip all of it by calling canSendSms directly.
- clients.communication_owner is always recomputed from evidence, never
  asserted by whichever trigger fired last, with a fixed priority to settle
  ties and an hourly reconcile.
- Cold copy is history-neutral. The Hub holds no conversation before
  2026-06-16 while records go back to 2023-09-15, so absence of a reply is a
  migration artifact, not proof nobody ever replied.
- Phase 2 exists. The owner was being assigned before the lane was built, so
  every finished listing campaign parked its lead somewhere permanently
  silent. rearmLane() means taking ownership also means giving the lane a
  next touch.
- A listing going under contract pulls the pivot forward instead of waiting
  for the lead's next scheduled slot, and renewed site activity enters a
  reactivation when it happens rather than when a sweep next runs.
- GET /api/ai/lanes/silent reports leads owned by a lane that is supposed to
  be talking to them with nothing scheduled, which is the one shape of bug
  that ownership made possible and no per-owner count would show.

45 new assertions. Verified against a clean worktree at HEAD: same three
pre-existing seller-campaign failures with and without these changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Emails sign Matt, and Day 0 goes back to the text we already had
entries.title: Emails sign Matt, and Day 0 goes back to the text we already had
entries.body:
John's three answers, 2026-10-23.

ALWAYS MATT ON ALL CAMPAIGNS. His written spec for this campaign signed
the emails "John"; asked about it he was unambiguous. That matches why the
rule exists: every outbound email leaves Matt's marketing address, so a
John sign-off confuses the reader, which is what happened to Rich Gholston
and Mark Herzberger. Two tests now hold it - the rendered email must sign
"Matt Smith / Matt Smith Team | RE/MAX Concepts" and the word John must
not appear anywhere in an email, body or sign-off. SMS stays John, because
that number is his.

RE/MAX CONCEPTS, with the slash, as his copy has it.

DAY 0 IS BACK TO THE OCTOBER 19 TEXT, website link included. I had
restated it to match the new spec's phrasing; "don't touch what we've
already built last time, this is just additional text and emails". So the
Day 0 message is frozen as approved, and everything in the response
campaign is additive to it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value Response Campaign: 13 steps, SMS and email alternating
entries.title: Home Value Response Campaign: 13 steps, SMS and email alternating
entries.body:
John's spec, 2026-10-23. This is the SHORT-TERM response and qualification
sequence that runs right after someone asks what their house is worth, not
the 26-email long-term nurture.

Day 1 email, 3 SMS, 5 email, 8 SMS, 11 email, 15 SMS, 19 email, 23 SMS,
28 email, 32 SMS, 37 email, then a soft close on both channels at Day 45.
Day 0 stays where it was: the valuation email, then the condition question
two minutes later.

The design point is that it does not ask for a listing appointment. It
asks the things an automated valuation cannot see - condition,
improvements, what a buyer would notice - and only raises a possible move
at DAY 15, once those questions have earned it. A test fails if any
question aimed at the homeowner's own plans appears before then.

The two channels do different jobs. The text asks one easy question; the
email that follows explains why that question matters. A test compares
each adjacent pair and fails if they duplicate.

Copy is John's VERBATIM, including where it opens mid-thought. The earlier
sequence rotated Hi/Hello/time-of-day in front of every message; this copy
does not want that, so nothing is prepended.

BLOCK RULES ARE NOW PER CHANNEL. The old ones were SMS-only, and applied
unchanged to email they were wrong four ways: a TEXT opt-out would silence
email, an undeliverable mobile would silence email, a homeowner with an
email and no phone would get nothing at all, and the "already texted in 20
hours" rule would hold back an email because of a text this very campaign
had just sent. A missing email now skips that one step instead of ending
the campaign, so a phone-only homeowner still gets every text.

Day 45 hands non-responders to the long-term nurture, drip 20 or drip 21
for past clients, and never restarts qualification.

THREE THINGS THAT NEED JOHN'S CALL, all deliberate in his spec and all
against a standing rule, so none were silently changed:
  1. These emails sign "John". Every other Hub email signs Matt, a rule
     added after two leads got John-signed mail from Matt's address.
  2. The copy writes "RE/MAX Concepts"; the spelling adopted 2026-10-16 is
     "REMAX Concepts" with no slash.
  3. The Day 0 text loses the website URL he added on 2026-10-19. The Day
     45 close still carries MattSmithTeam.com.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Registered sorts by time within a day, and shows it
entries.title: Registered sorts by time within a day, and shows it
entries.body:
John: "the registered sort column needs to know time too, so when I sort,
the most recent on the same day would show at the very top."

register_date is a DATE with no time. The five leads off the Ranmar ad all
carried "2026-10-23", so they tied on the only key the sort had and came
back in whatever order SQLite chose. They landed OLDEST first under a
newest-first sort, which is the complaint.

Now the sort takes the calendar DAY from whichever source supplied it,
then breaks the tie on the most precise timestamp that row actually has,
then on id so the order is total and a refresh never reshuffles equal
rows. oldest_first mirrors it exactly, so flipping the column reverses
what you were looking at instead of producing a different order.

Two details found by running it against the real data rather than
reasoning about it:

The day is compared through substr, because a row with a bare date and a
row with a full timestamp are otherwise judged on different things and
anything lacking register_date outranks the entire day.

The separator is normalised. Sierra writes "2026-10-23T19:07:32" and the
Hub writes "2026-10-23 19:46:09" with a space, and a space sorts below "T"
as a string, so a 7:46pm lead was landing beneath a 7:07pm one. Caught
because the test used both shapes.

The column now prints the time beside the date. The sort breaks ties on it,
so the column should be able to explain its own order rather than be
argued with.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: The "Form" fix was dead on arrival; five leads went out wrong
entries.title: The "Form" fix was dead on arrival; five leads went out wrong
entries.body:
John: "look at what you sent, make sure it never happens again, do not
include the word form and just use the property address."

The cleaner I shipped two hours ago never ran. A heredoc turned the \b in
its regex into a literal backspace byte, so the pattern was anchored on
0x08 and matched nothing. It read correctly in every normal view of the
file, passed a test that re-declared the regex instead of calling the real
one, and silently did nothing in production.

So David Stickley, Randy Roe, Doug Farley and Danielle Hamilton were all
told "You were looking at 1625 Ranmar Dr Ely Form on Facebook", three of
them AFTER the fix deployed.

Two faults, both fixed properly:

WRONG PLACE. The cleaner sat in fub-leads.js, which is one of three
callers of ingestFbLead; routes/clients.js and the events path were never
covered. It now lives in lead-intake.js and runs INSIDE ingestFbLead, the
single point every caller passes through. One definition, no duplicate to
drift: fub-leads imports it.

WRONG TEST. The old test grepped the source and re-declared the regex
inline, so it passed while the shipped code was dead. The tests now import
and call the real function, and one asserts the source contains no control
characters, because a backspace in a regex is invisible in every normal
readout.

Noticed while scanning for the same damage, NOT fixed here and not mine:
server/fsbo-master.js, server/fub-status-push.js and server/routes/admin.js
each carry the identical 0x08-for-\b corruption in live regexes, so FSBO
address normalisation, the SOI stage match and the admin address cleaner
have silently never worked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: The preflight was reading a key that does not exist
entries.title: The preflight was reading a key that does not exist
entries.body:
It reported "the whole Facebook lead pipeline is dead" while two leads
were flowing through it perfectly.

The switch is fub_lead_email_enabled, with the u. The preflight I wrote an
hour earlier read fb_lead_email_enabled without it, found nothing, took
the '0' default and announced a blocker. David Stickley and Brytta
Fitzgibbons had both arrived through that exact path forty minutes before,
their notes still carrying the fub_email markers that prove it.

A preflight exists to be trusted when it says something is broken. One
that cries wolf from a typo is worse than not having it, so the key is no
longer spelled in two places: fub-leads.js owns the switch and exports
fubLeadEmailEnabled(), and the preflight asks it.

Also corrects the commit before this one. The readiness route was NOT
being shadowed by /fb-campaign/:clientId. It returned 404 because the
deploy was genuinely slow, and it answered correctly from its original
position once that deploy landed - a minute before the reordering commit
was even written, which is what gives it away. Keeping the route above the
parameterised one is still right, but the reason given was wrong.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: The preflight route was being swallowed by /fb-campaign/:clientId
entries.title: The preflight route was being swallowed by /fb-campaign/:clientId
entries.body:
It returned 404 for twenty-five minutes and I kept reading that as a slow
deploy. It was not: Express matches the FIRST route that fits, and
'/fb-campaign/:clientId' sat above it, so a request for
'/fb-campaign/readiness' was handled as a campaign lookup for a client
called "readiness".

Third time this exact shape has bitten in one session, after /email-cap
and /resync-schedule. The route now sits above the parameterised one, and
the reason is written next to it so the next person moving code around
does not quietly undo it.

entries.subject: Don't cold-open a lead someone already called, and drop "Form"
entries.title: Don't cold-open a lead someone already called, and drop "Form"
entries.body:
The Ranmar ad went live at 1:46 PM and produced its first lead inside
half an hour. Both faults showed up on that one lead.

HUMAN SPOKE FIRST, AI TEXTED ANYWAY. David Stickley arrived at 2:08:23,
John called him at 2:08:52, and the AI texted "Is there anything you'd
like to know about the home?" at 2:13:55 - five minutes after a call it
knew nothing about. Every guard in the AI watches for an INBOUND reply,
which is the wrong direction: a call John places leaves an OUTGOING row
and nothing was reading it. The opener and its ten-minute follow-up email
now both ask whether a human on our side has already made contact since
the lead arrived, and stand down if so, handing the lead to HUMAN_TAKEOVER
rather than talking over a conversation already in progress.

Checked twice rather than once, because the email is queued ten minutes
ahead and that is ample time for someone to pick up the phone in between.

THE WORD "FORM" REACHED A CUSTOMER. Facebook lead forms are NAMED after
the listing they advertise, so the form name is "1625 Ranmar Dr Ely Form"
and that string is the listing label. David was told "You were looking at
1625 Ranmar Dr Ely Form on Facebook". It is also the CRM tag and the label
every one of the eight 30-day steps prints. cleanListingLabel trims the
words that make it a form name, and only at the END, so a street that
genuinely contains one of them stays intact: "12 Form Street" is untouched.

Tests pin both in the direction that actually failed: an outgoing call
counts, an agent's own text counts, the AI's own text does not (or it
would silence itself), an inbound message is not outreach, and contact
from before the lead existed is a different conversation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Preflight: would a lead off this listing ad actually be handled?
entries.title: Preflight: would a lead off this listing ad actually be handled?
entries.body:
John launched 1625 Ranmar Dr Ely today and asked for the messaging and
follow-up to be set up the way Springville was.

The pipeline behind a listing ad is four separate things, and each of them
fails silently: the FUB lead EMAIL trigger, the Gmail poller that reads
it, the approved opener bank, and the 30-day campaign with its
property-status check. On Springville a Gmail filter quietly filed the
lead emails under a label that skipped the inbox, the poller saw nothing,
and two real leads were missed before anyone noticed. An ad spends money
from the moment it goes live, so "probably wired up" is not good enough.

GET /api/ai/fb-campaign/readiness?listing=... answers one question: if a
lead came in off this listing right now, would anything happen. It reports
the trigger switch, the campaign switch, the connected mailboxes, the
opener count, and anyone already enrolled, then names the blockers in
plain language rather than leaving a reader to interpret four booleans.

It checks the listing TRANSACTION specifically, because the status check
is only as good as the transaction behind it. No match means the campaign
cannot tell active from sold, which is exactly how a house under contract
keeps being pitched as available.

Read-only. No sends. Safe to run before every launch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Read-only: what texting actually cost, from Twilio's records
entries.title: Read-only: what texting actually cost, from Twilio's records
entries.body:
John: "Is the MMS costing us more? like the group text from yesterday
with Melena and Matt, or was that just normal texting?"

A fair question with a non-obvious answer, and nothing in the Hub could
reach the billing figures to settle it.

Group texting is MMS by protocol, not by choice. Twilio: "Group texting,
or more specifically Group MMS, uses the Multimedia Messaging Service
(MMS) protocol to exchange ordinary text messages among a group of three
or more people." So a group text is billed as MMS even carrying no
picture at all, which is why the breakdown separates "MMS (no media)"
from "MMS (with media)" rather than assuming media means MMS.

A group also bills PER RECIPIENT. One message to a group of two is two
billed messages. The Hub shows that as a single row, so the cost is easy
to underestimate by exactly the size of the group.

This reports Twilio's own `price` field rather than estimating from a
rate card, so it is what was charged, not what we think the rate is.
Price lands a little after the send, so the newest messages can read null
and are counted separately instead of being silently treated as free.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Texting a number that belongs to a lead now reaches the lead
entries.title: Texting a number that belongs to a lead now reaches the lead
entries.body:
John: "he did reply on this but it does not sync with my previous text to
Josh, I texted him separately as a number."

Josh the inspector was already in the CRM, record 35885. Texting him by
number logged the send against client_id NULL in thread u_3193897599,
while his reply matched his record and landed on his profile. One
conversation in two places, neither half showing the other.

The raw-phone branch carried the comment "no CRM record, no consumer
compliance gate", which is only true while the first half holds. It never
checked. So the threading bug had a second, worse face: if the number
belonged to someone who had replied STOP, typing it by hand sent to them
anyway. An opt-out that a keystroke can walk around is not an opt-out.

Now the number is resolved against clients first, by primary and alt
phone. A match is treated as the person they are: their STOP is honoured,
an undeliverable number is refused with the same wording as anywhere else,
the message is logged against their record in their own thread, and the AI
stands down exactly as it would for any other human send. Only a genuine
stranger takes the ungated path, which is what that path was always for.

The existing split conversation was repaired separately with
/unknown/relink-all, which found Josh and left the other 14 unknown
threads alone because no client matches them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: New Message can attach photos to a text
entries.title: New Message can attach photos to a text
entries.body:
John, right after the non-contact texting fix: "on the text to those that
are not on our list we should be able to add image to."

Nothing new was needed underneath. The send route already forwards `media`
to Twilio as MMS, and it does it for raw phone recipients on the same
footing as CRM leads, so an inspector gets a photo exactly as a client
would. The reply box inside a thread already had a working uploader. The
New Message composer was simply the one place that had never been given
one.

So this reuses that path rather than inventing a second: the same
/api/inbox/upload-media call, the same thumbnail strip with a remove
button, the same ten-photo ceiling. The picker only appears on the text
channel, because an email attachment goes to SendGrid a different way and
pretending otherwise would be a quiet failure.

Also relaxed the send guard. It demanded body text, which would have
rejected a photo sent on its own - a perfectly ordinary thing to do when
you are showing a contractor what you are looking at. The route already
allowed it; now the UI does too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: New Message can text a number that is not in the CRM
entries.title: New Message can text a number that is not in the CRM
entries.body:
John: "the separate new message texting anyone that is not on our contact
list is not working, that should function like a normal text, only
difference is those people we will be texting are not in our list."

Two things were wrong and only one of them was obvious.

The button was hardcoded `disabled={sending || channel === 'text'}` and
labelled "Text (needs Twilio)". It never checked Twilio at all. The label
was left over from before Twilio was connected, so the Text option in New
Message has never worked, long after texting started working everywhere
else in the Hub.

Underneath that, the composer could only address CRM records: it searched
clients and posted client_ids, so typing an inspector's number found
nothing and offered nothing. The API has accepted raw `phones` all along,
with a comment about "team agents not in the CRM" - it sends them, logs
them under thread_key u_<digits> with a null client_id, and attaches the
same delivery status callback. Only the UI had no way to offer it.

Now a typed 10 or 11 digit number appears in the dropdown as "Text
+1319...", Enter accepts it, and the chip says "not a contact" so nobody
mistakes it for a lead. Raw recipients post as `phones` and clients still
post as `client_ids`, so a single message can go to both.

The recipients carry a negative id, which cannot collide with a client id
and keeps removal working without a second list to track.

Also: the text path no longer demands a subject. That check was written
for email and silently blocked every text, which would have been the next
thing to break once the button was clickable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: A sent group text now says whether it arrived
entries.title: A sent group text now says whether it arrived
entries.body:
John, looking at the first real group send: "there's no receipt though on
text if it was delivered or not." The thread showed "no receipt" while
Twilio had "delivered" for both recipients the whole time.

A 1:1 text gets its status from Twilio's status webhook, matched on
external_id = 'twilio_' + the SM... SID. A group text goes out through the
Conversations API, which returns an IM... SID and fires no such webhook.
The row is stored as 'conv_' + IM..., so the webhook has nothing to match
and delivery_status stays empty forever. Everything needed was already on
the row; nothing ever asked Twilio for the answer.

reconcileGroupReceipts asks. A pull rather than a webhook because receipts
land a few seconds after the send and Conversations offers no callback for
them. The send schedules its own check 25 seconds out, and a 10-minute
sweep is the backstop for anything that missed, including sends made while
the Hub was restarting.

A group has several recipients and the Hub has one row, so the status is a
summary: delivered only when everyone got it, partial when some did,
undelivered when nobody did. Partial also records WHO missed it, because
"partial" with no names is the same dead end as no receipt at all.

Also corrected a comment that my own earlier change made false. It still
told the reader a phone can only be in one group at a time, which was the
reason the 1:1 copy fallback existed. That ceiling is gone; the fallback
now covers genuine failures only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: The Hub has to be IN the group before it can post to one
entries.title: The Hub has to be IN the group before it can post to one
entries.body:
John hit it on the first real send: "Group text failed: Message author
should be among group MMS participants."

The conversation and every member were created correctly. The send failed
because a group MMS message must be authored BY a participant, and the
Hub was passing the display string "Matt Smith Team", which is nobody.

This is what ProjectedAddress is actually for, and what an earlier attempt
got backwards by attaching it to phone numbers, which returns 50407. It is
the mask for a CHAT identity: "a projected address represents a non-native
(such as Chat) Participant so every member of a group text can see who
sent each message." So the Hub joins the conversation as the identity
matt-smith-team wearing our Twilio number, and is then allowed to speak.
One stable identity, so every group shows the same sender.

ensureHubSeat is idempotent, because the same rule bites on the follow-up
path too: sendConversationMessage had the identical bug, so the first
message would have failed and every later message into an existing group
would have failed the same way. An existing seat counts as success, which
also lets an older group be posted into once a seat is added.

If the seat cannot be taken, the new conversation is deleted rather than
left behind. A group nobody can post into is worse than no group.

The author parameter is gone from both functions. It was dead once the
identity became the author, and leaving it would invite someone to set a
sender that Twilio will reject.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Group texts: drop the proxy address, which was the whole ceiling
entries.title: Group texts: drop the proxy address, which was the whole ceiling
entries.body:
Twilio's rule, verbatim: "The same person (i.e., a single personal phone
number) can be part of any number of conversations concurrently, as long
as the address they are in contact with (the ProxyAddress) is unique."

With one sending number that reads as one group per person, and the old
code honoured it by evicting people from their earlier group - silently.
That is how four of our nine groups came to reach the wrong people, and
why adding Matt to a new group kept knocking him out of the last one.

The group-texting guide gives the other form: "You only have to specify
the SMS participant's own personal phone number in
MessagingBinding.Address. When using group texting, you won't need to
specify proxy addresses." A participant added that way has no proxy, so
the uniqueness rule has nothing to bite on.

Proven live before changing anything: in a throwaway Conversations
Service, the same mobile was added to two conversations on this one
number, the second add returned 201, and the first conversation still
listed them afterwards. The live Lucas Pietan conversation was read
before and after and was untouched.

Also gone: the proxy POOL, the twilio_group_proxy_numbers setting and the
conversation-scanning picker. They existed to buy our way around the
ceiling with extra numbers. The ceiling is gone, so they are moot, and
nothing needs purchasing.

The eviction fallback goes too. Without a proxy there is no
cross-conversation conflict to resolve, so a failed add is now a real
failure and is reported rather than papered over by moving someone.

Still unproven: DELIVERY. This was a binding test and sent no messages.
One real send to team phones is the remaining step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Remove my duplicate text alert, and ask SendGrid what it actually did
entries.title: my duplicate text alert, and ask SendGrid what it actually did
entries.body:
Two things, both from John's screenshot showing Matt receiving TWO emails for one text.

1. The email alert for an inbound text has existed all along - notifyInboundText() in
   routes/inbox.js, called from the SMS webhook and both group-text paths. Yesterday I
   searched for the sender, missed it, concluded the Hub had never sent one, and added a
   second. Matt got both. Mine is removed; there is one alert in one place again.

2. John is NOT suppressed at SendGrid - bounces, blocks, spam reports, invalid addresses
   and global unsubscribes all came back clean for his address and Matt's. Both recipient
   settings are absent, so the defaults apply and he IS addressed. isBlockedEmail only
   filters throwaway domains, and both are gmail.com. So the Hub sends to both and
   SendGrid accepts both, which moves the question to what SendGrid DID with it.

   /api/admin/email-deliverability now also reports SendGrid's per-message activity -
   delivered, deferred, bounced, dropped. That needs the Email Activity add-on, so a
   401/403 is reported as a plan limit rather than mistaken for an answer.

entries.subject: Louder text chirp
entries.title: Louder text chirp
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-21: "make the text message sound a little more louder". 0.18 -> 0.42.

Loudness here is amplitude, not duration: the two notes stay short, so it carries across
a room without becoming something you switch off by Wednesday. The test now asserts a
range rather than a literal, since the exact number is a taste setting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Probe the add format instead of assuming it
entries.title: Probe the add format instead of assuming it
entries.body:
The first run sent MessagingBinding.ProjectedAddress with a real mobile
number and got 50407 on every add, including the first, so it tested
nothing. That was my error: ProjectedAddress is the mask for a CHAT
participant with an Identity - "a projected address represents a
non-native (such as Chat) Participant" - not a way to add a phone number.

Twilio documents two different forms for a native SMS participant and
they disagree with each other. The Group Texting guide says "You only
have to specify the SMS participant's own personal phone number in
MessagingBinding.Address. When using group texting, you won't need to
specify proxy addresses." The Participant resource page says Address AND
ProxyAddress are both required.

That disagreement is the whole question, because the documented ceiling
is phrased in terms of the proxy: "The same person can be part of any
number of conversations concurrently, as long as the address they are in
contact with (the ProxyAddress) is unique." If a group participant has no
proxy, that rule cannot bite.

So this version tries address-only first, falls back to address+proxy,
reports which Twilio actually accepted, and only then asks the real
question with whichever form worked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Check whether SendGrid is refusing an address
entries.title: Check whether SendGrid is refusing an address
entries.body:
Matt receives the text-notification emails and John does not, while both recipient
settings sit on their defaults - so the Hub IS addressing him and the problem is
delivery. One suppressed address on a multi-recipient send is dropped silently while the
others arrive, which is exactly that shape.

GET /api/admin/email-deliverability?email= checks SendGrid's bounces, blocks, spam
reports, invalid addresses and global unsubscribes, plus what the Hub's own log says it
sent there. Read-only: lifting a suppression is a separate deliberate act and is not done
here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Diagnostic: can one number hold a person in two Group MMS groups
entries.title: Diagnostic: can one number hold a person in two Group MMS groups
entries.body:
The whole group-texting rebuild rests on one fact Twilio does not
document, and the documented evidence points two ways.

50416, the rule we hit today, says a participant+proxy pair conflicts
with any "active conversation" - across conversations. That is why adding
Matt to a second group evicts him from the first; createGroupText binds
people with MessagingBinding.ProxyAddress.

50437, the Group MMS equivalent, scopes every cause "in this
conversation", including "A native GMMS Participant with the same Address
exists in this conversation". No cross-conversation rule is documented for
Group MMS at all.

So the case for Group MMS rests on the absence of a rule rather than the
presence of one, which is not good enough to rebuild on.

This settles it empirically. It sends NO messages - the conflict fires
when a participant is added, not when one is sent - so the question can be
answered without texting anybody. It works inside a throwaway Conversations
Service and deletes it in a finally block. It also reads the live
conversation holding Matt before and after, so if a Group MMS add disturbs
an existing proxy binding we learn that here rather than in front of a
client.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Show who actually receives each Hub alert
entries.title: Show who actually receives each Hub alert
entries.body:
Matt was getting text-notification emails and John was not. The recipients come from
app_settings values that merely DEFAULT to John's address, so once inbox_notify_email was
written to something else the default stopped applying - and nothing in any screen showed
it, which is why this took a code read to answer.

GET /api/admin/notify-recipients reports each setting, whether it is still on its
default, and the resulting recipient list per alert type. Read-only; addresses only.

entries.subject: A new text makes a sound, and now sends an email that never existed
entries.title: A new text makes a sound, and now sends an email that never existed
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-21, two things.

1. A chirp when a text arrives. Synthesised with WebAudio rather than shipped as an audio
   file: nothing to host, nothing for a content policy to block, no load delay before the
   first one plays. Two short rising notes, the second higher and shorter, which is what
   makes it read as a chirp rather than a beep; quiet and under a third of a second,
   because it fires while someone is working.

   Only a genuinely NEW inbound text chirps. /unread-count now reports the newest unread
   notification, so the bell knows WHAT arrived - a backup report or a campaign response
   raises the badge silently. The first poll seeds the marker instead of firing for
   everything already waiting, so opening the Hub with unread texts is silent. Mute is a
   per-browser toggle in the bell menu, and switching it on plays the chirp, which both
   previews it and satisfies the browser rule that audio needs a user gesture.

2. "Why did the text notification email not go to johnwithmattsmithteam@gmail.com?"
   Because no address was wrong: the Hub had never sent one. An inbound text raised the
   in-app bell and a web push and stopped there - notify() writes a row and pushes, it
   does not email. notifyNewInbound is only ever called for the EMAIL channel. Whatever
   text alerts he had been getting came from another system.

   notifyNewText now emails on an inbound text, to the same recipients the inbound-email
   alert uses - John and Matt always, plus the same configurable extras - with the message
   in the subject so it reads from a lock screen. Settable off with
   text_notify_email_enabled. Fire-and-forget, so it can never hold up storing the message
   or the campaign guards below it.

test/text-notification.test.mjs (17).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Re-sync must not push a seller's FIRST text
entries.title: Re-sync must not push a seller's FIRST text
entries.body:
Caught by the first dry run against production, which is what dry runs are
for. Seven sellers with attempt_count 0 were due Text 1 the next morning
and the re-sync proposed moving them to Nov 4, a fortnight later, because
scheduleNextFsbo(0) falls through to the 15-day branch.

The cadence governs the gap BETWEEN texts. Enrolment dates the first one.
A row with nothing sent yet is now reported as skipped_not_yet_texted and
left exactly where it was.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: FSBO: re-date rows still waiting on the old cadence
entries.title: FSBO: re-date rows still waiting on the old cadence
entries.body:
scheduleNextFsbo only decides the gap AFTER a text sends, so moving Text 2
to DOM 30 left every already-booked row on the old clock. Three sellers
had Text 2 sitting at the old +7 and would have been texted at DOM 20.

Pause/resume cannot fix it: resume sets next_send_at to the next valid
slot, which sends immediately - the opposite of the problem.

POST /api/lists/fsbo/campaign/resync-schedule recomputes next_send_at
under the CURRENT rule, measured from the last text actually sent rather
than from today, so a re-sync never silently restarts a seller's clock.

DRY BY DEFAULT, and it will only push a text LATER unless allow_earlier
is sent explicitly. Pulling one earlier means texting a real person
sooner than they were promised to be left alone, which is a decision, not
a correction. Only 'active' rows are considered, so a paused or removed
lead can never be re-dated back into the queue.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: FSBO: Text 2 moves to DOM 30, the analysis pair is cut, then 15/15/30
entries.title: FSBO: Text 2 moves to DOM 30, the analysis pair is cut, then 15/15/30
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-20: "move text 2 on the 30th day DOM then remove the 2
part text 3 then next text again would be after 15 days 2 15 days then
move to 30."

The sequence is now:

  Text 1   DOM >= 14    availability check
  Text 2   DOM 30       still-available check
  Text 3   +15 days     availability rotation
  Text 4   +15 days     availability rotation
  then     every ~30d   availability rotation

Text 2 is a position on the listing's clock rather than a gap, which
needed a floor. On the day this changed, 26 of the 40 eligible sellers
were ALREADY past DOM 30 and several were past DOM 300, so their Text 2
was due in the past - it would have gone out in the same sweep as Text 1,
two cold texts back to back. The floor is 15 days, John's own rhythm from
the rest of this sequence, and it costs nothing normally: a seller who
enrols at the DOM 14 threshold still lands on DOM 29-30. An unknown or
zero DOM falls back to the threshold assumption rather than to zero.

The market-analysis pair is gone. Its opening credibility block came out
on 2026-10-05, which left the survivor starting "At this point," - a
reference to weeks that no longer appeared anywhere. Rather than reword a
dangling sentence the whole step is removed, so attempt 3 onward draws
from the plain availability rotation like every later touch. Nothing in
the sequence pitches an analysis any more. The two-texts-apart sender
existed only for that pair and went with it; every step is one text now.

Three leads already have Text 2 scheduled on the old +7 rule and will be
re-dated separately - the code only decides the NEXT gap, never a row
already waiting.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Import Matt's calendar unfiltered, titles as he wrote them
entries.title: Import Matt's calendar unfiltered, titles as he wrote them
entries.body:
The allow-list shipped an hour ago is removed. John's call, and the
reasoning is sound: the only thing separating "Mike O podiatrist" from
"Showing Confirmed" is a guess at the wording, and Google carries no
reliable signal to do better. visibility=private is set on 18 of the 31
real showings and on only 7 of the 45 other events, so leaning on it
would hide the appointments and leak the rest - precisely backwards.
colorId is unset on all 76 events. transparency means busy/free.

Labelling the remainder "Busy - personal" was the alternative and it was
rejected for the right reason: we would be asserting something we cannot
check. "Need to send my EO into the commission" and "4th Quarter Blitz"
are work, not personal.

So the Hub mirrors the calendar as it is. Matt's calendar stays the
master; everything deleted from the Hub returns on the next sync, because
nothing was ever removed from Google.

Cancelled events are still skipped. That is not a content filter - an
event carrying STATUS:CANCELLED is not happening, and showing it as live
is simply wrong data.

The timezone fix and its 10 tests are untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Import Matt's calendar in Central, 12-hour, appointments only
entries.title: Import Matt's calendar in Central, 12-hour, appointments only
entries.body:
The iCal import went live today and pulled 74 events off Matt's primary
calendar. Three things were wrong with what landed.

Times were 5 hours late. Google sends DTSTART:20261022T140000Z and
parseICalDate matched only the digits, discarding the trailing Z, so UTC
was stored as if it were Central. Every timed event was wrong and one
evening showing had already slid onto the following day. The conversion
now goes through the America/Chicago zone rather than a fixed -5, so it
follows the DST switch by itself: a 14:00Z event reads 9:00am in October
and 8:00am in December. Floating and TZID times are already local and are
left alone; all-day events keep their date.

The calendar showed 24-hour times. Stored values stay 24-hour, because
that is what sorts in SQL and what <input type="time"> needs, but the
month and day views now render 12-hour.

48 of the 74 events were nobody else's business. Matt's primary calendar
is his whole life: a podiatrist appointment, a massage, two haircuts, a
personal legal deadline with a case number, and a run of marketing
webinars, all landing on a calendar the whole team reads. The import is
now an allow-list, not a block-list, and it fails closed - a title has to
look like a real estate appointment to come through. Leaking a medical
appointment to the team costs more than the Hub missing an event Matt can
still see in Google. Cancelled events are skipped too; they stay in the
feed carrying STATUS:CANCELLED and we were importing them as live.

Tested against the 47 distinct titles the live feed actually produced:
14 come through, 33 stay out.

Known gaps, not addressed here: recurring events still import only their
first occurrence, and events deleted in Google are never pruned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Correct the reply handler's own doc comment
entries.title: the reply handler's own doc comment
entries.body:
The file header was updated when a reply stopped ending the campaign, but
handleFsboReply's own comment still said "RESPONSE STOPS AUTOMATION FIRST ... (John,
2026-09-14)" - the opposite of what the function now does.
