entries.subject: An FSBO reply no longer ends the campaign
entries.title: An FSBO reply no longer ends the campaign
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-20: "even when we get a response the campaign should still be on, please
make sure FSBO campaign is only turned off if it was manually done."

This reverses his own 2026-09-14 rule, under which any inbound reply moved the record to
'responded' and cleared next_send_at. A seller answering a question is engagement, not a
reason to go quiet on them. A person still answers every reply personally - there are
still no automated replies of any kind - but the schedule now carries on underneath.

It was five places, not one: the reply handler, the eligibility check, the prior-reply
history scan, the inbound-since-enrollment safety net, and a migration that stamped every
replier as 'responded'. All five now consult one exported list.

Four things still end a campaign, and only four:
  - a human pausing or removing it
  - an explicit STOP (legal, not a preference)
  - a DISQUALIFYING_REPLY: wrong number, sold, rented, listed with an agent, holding,
    not interested. Continuing past these would be wrong rather than merely persistent -
    we would be texting the wrong person, or a house that is not theirs to sell, or
    someone who has said no.
  - the listing leaving the market

The response task and notification now say the campaign is still running, since the old
wording told the team the opposite.

Also adds reactivateRespondedFsbo (POST /api/lists/fsbo/campaign/reactivate-responded,
DRY BY DEFAULT) to return the 27 records the old rule froze out. It is deliberately not a
blanket undo: a disqualifying stored response_class stays off, and anyone opted out is
untouched. Resumed sends trickle ~3 minutes apart.

test/fsbo-reply-keeps-campaign.test.mjs (15). S5, S10 and the no-auto-reply test are
updated to the new rule; the invariant that nothing is ever sent back automatically is
unchanged and still passing. 79 FSBO tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Add the website to the Day 0 home value text
entries.title: the website to the Day 0 home value text
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-19. Appended to the condition question, after the ask, so
the question still leads.

Written as the FULL https://www.mattsmithteam.com/ rather than a bare
www. domain, which a lot of handsets render as plain text rather than a
tappable link. Same reason the buyer nurture uses the full form on its
Day 1 message.

Checked the cost before adding it: rendered for a real lead the message
goes from 333 to 364 characters, which is 3 GSM-7 segments either way.
Even a long name and a long street address stays at 3. A test pins
that, so a future edit that tips it to 4 fails rather than quietly
costing more on every send.

Still exactly ONE url, which is the standing SMS rule. The test that
used to assert zero links now asserts exactly one, and that it is the
full form.

15 tests on the Day 0 message, 48 across both home value suites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Alternate the greeting across the home value texts
entries.title: Alternate the greeting across the home value texts
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-19: "use alternate hi, hello and time of day".

Rotated by STEP INDEX rather than through the global {{intro}} counter,
so one lead is guaranteed to see all three across their sequence
instead of whatever that counter happened to be on when their turn
came round.

Day 0 keeps "Hi", which is John's approved wording, so the rotation
starts at Hello on Day 3 and the run reads:
  Hi, Hello, time-of-day, Hi, Hello, time-of-day, Hi, Hello

Never "Good evening": the sending window closes at 5pm, so it could
only ever be wrong. Morning or afternoon only, asserted across the day.

The tests caught a real one while being updated: a caller that forgot
to pass a greeting rendered "undefined Dana,". Defended in the step
itself rather than only in the callers, so no future path can ship that
to a phone.

33 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value: the 45 day SMS follow-up, Days 3 to 45
entries.title: Home Value: the 45 day SMS follow-up, Days 3 to 45
entries.body:
John's spec, 2026-10-19. An EXTENSION of the existing Home Value
Request workflow, not a second campaign: the email and the Day 0
condition question stay where they are in home-value-intake.js and are
not duplicated. This picks up at Day 3.

Seven steps on the days specified - 3, 7, 12, 18, 25, 35, 45 - each
asking for one thing an automated estimate cannot see: improvements,
motivation, condition, unusual features, finished square footage. The
walkthrough is offered ONCE, at Day 35, as a way to make the number
more accurate rather than as a listing pitch. Day 45 leaves the door
open and the sequence completes.

Day offsets are measured from the original REQUEST, not from the last
send, so a weekend delay does not push everything after it.

ANY REPLY ENDS IT: a rating, a question, an objection, a wrong number.
The sequence stops, every queued text is cancelled (including a Day 0
question that has not fired), the lead moves to HUMAN_TAKEOVER, a
person is notified, and the AI is blocked. routes/inbox.js now gates
the AI hand-off on hvLead the same way it does cxLead and fsboLead, and
for the same reason: a fire-and-forget call there would let the AI
answer before the campaign had stopped.

A 1-to-10 reply is parsed and stored, and the agent is shown John's
suggested follow-up for that band. SUGGESTIONS ONLY, never sent.

Also fixes the Day 0 timing to John's spec: two minutes, but inside the
permitted weekday window, queued for the next permitted time if the
email went out after hours. That replaces the quiet-hours-only rule I
shipped this morning.

CUSTOM FIELDS VERIFIED BOTH WAYS, since two mechanisms are in play.
Day 0 uses {{first_name}}/{{street_address}} through fillTemplate; Days
3+ substitute in code. Checked against awkward records - no name, name
is "None", name is an email address, no address, neither - and every
one resolves with a natural fallback ("Hi there", "your home"). No raw
token, "undefined" or "None" can reach a phone.

Third instance today of Number(null) being 0 and passing isFinite: a
lead with NO rating was being shown the "rated 1 to 4" suggestions.
Validate, do not coerce.

28 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Condition question, texted two minutes after the home value email
entries.title: Condition question, texted two minutes after the home value email
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-19, his wording verbatim. They have just asked what the
house is worth, so they are at the keyboard, and condition is the one
thing an online estimate cannot see. A 1-to-10 answer is one tap.

Only fires behind a SUCCESSFUL email. If the email did not go, the text
would thank them for a request they never saw us answer.

TIMING: two minutes, unless that lands in quiet hours, in which case it
waits for the morning. Deliberately NOT pushed to the next weekday
9-to-5 slot the way proactive prospecting is. This is a reply to
something they did themselves minutes ago, and holding a Saturday
enquiry until Monday throws away the reason for sending it. Quiet hours
are the boundary that matters, not the working week.

Rides the existing scheduled_texts runner, so compliance is re-checked
AT SEND TIME, not just now: STOP, Junk/DNC, undeliverable number, and a
skip if the AI or a person is mid-conversation. Queueing also checks
STOP and undeliverable up front, so an obvious case never enters the
queue at all.

ONCE PER PERSON, EVER. A second or third home value request is a strong
signal that deserves a person, not the same canned question again.

No phone is a normal outcome for a web form, not an error: it returns a
reason and queues nothing.

Straight apostrophes, asserted by test. One curly apostrophe would push
this 330-character message out of GSM-7 and into UCS-2, turning three
segments into seven.

13 tests. Delay is a dial (home_value_question_delay_minutes, 2).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: A manual enrol on an untagged lead now asks before texting them
entries.title: A manual enrol on an untagged lead now asks before texting them
entries.body:
John asked what I recommend. This: close the one way past the
cancellation hold before using it on Stephen Walters, so the order of
two clicks stops deciding whether a real person gets an unwanted text.

The 48 hour hold reads mls_status and off_market_date. A lead the
master file has not caught up with has neither, so the hold has nothing
to measure and they look like any ordinary lead. Enrol them by hand
today and they are texted today, which is exactly what the rule exists
to prevent. Simulated against Stephen's real record: as he stands now
the verdict is ELIGIBLE and he would be texted at the next weekday
slot; with the master file refreshed it is TOO_SOON_AFTER_CANCEL,
holding to the 21st.

Auto-enrolment never had this exposure, because an untagged lead is not
in the Cancelled/Expired list to begin with. Only Resume/Re-enroll
could reach it.

Both manual paths now return needs_override with a reason naming the
fix, the same shape Send-AI-now uses, so a deliberate yes still works
and is recorded. Narrow on purpose: it takes BOTH fields missing, so a
legacy lead carrying either one is unaffected, and the bulk path is
untouched.

29 tests, including one asserting auto-enrolment still works and one
asserting the override does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: The 48 hour cancel hold now applies only under 90 days on market
entries.title: The 48 hour cancel hold now applies only under 90 days on market
entries.body:
John's full rule, finished. The daily expired/cancelled pipeline added
real DOM and List Date columns to the master sheet this morning (115 of
257 rows populated, all plain integers, verified against the live
sheet), so the condition I said was unachievable is now buildable.

I was wrong about that, and it is worth recording why: DOM was already
in the Notes blob 116 times as "DOM 31" with no colon. I searched for
"DOM:" and concluded it did not exist. A peer session caught it.

Now:
  Cancelled + DOM under 90   -> hold 48 hours
  Cancelled + DOM 90 or more -> no hold, text on the normal schedule
  Cancelled + DOM unknown    -> hold (74 of 107 cancelled rows have no
                                DOM, and 28 of the 33 that do are under
                                90, so short is both likelier and safer)
  Expired, any DOM           -> no hold, as asked

clients.mls_dom and clients.mls_list_date are written by the master
sync, by header NAME, and only when the sheet has a value - blanking a
known DOM because an older row came through empty would lose the one
field this rule depends on.

Two bugs caught before they shipped:

1. My first version returned ok:true for a long listing, which would
   have jumped every remaining eligibility check below it - junk
   status, opt-outs, reply history. A long DOM now skips the HOLD, not
   the checks.
2. Number(null) is 0 and 0 is finite, so an unknown DOM read as "nought
   days on market". DOM 0 is a real value in this data (a listing
   pulled the day it went live), so unknown and zero have to stay
   distinguishable. Same coercion-versus-validation trap the rules
   stress test caught in setRule last week.

A placeholder-count check also caught the INSERT gaining two columns
without two more question marks.

24 tests on this rule, 51 across the related suites.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Block a lead from the C/E campaign BEFORE they are enrolled
entries.title: Block a lead from the C/E campaign BEFORE they are enrolled
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-19: "make sure that Stephen Walters does not get any
text first".

removeFromCampaign was a bare UPDATE, so for somebody not yet enrolled
it silently did nothing. That is exactly when you most want to stop
them: the lead you want protected is usually the one the master file is
about to sweep in an hour from now.

It upserts now. A human 'removed' row is written in advance, and
enrollClient already refuses paused/removed rows, so the auto-enrol
tick will not pick them up for a first text.

Same lesson as the FSBO pre-enrolment exclusion and the AI
never-contact list: a block that only works after the thing exists is
not a block.

2 tests, one for each direction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Hold a cancelled listing for 48 hours before the first text
entries.title: Hold a cancelled listing for 48 hours before the first text
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-19. Cancelling is a decision somebody made this week,
often mid-conversation with their own agent. Texting the next morning
reads as having watched the MLS rather than having noticed them.

EXPIRED IS EXEMPT, as asked: an expired listing reached the end of a
term set months earlier, so there is no fresh decision to intrude on.
mls_status distinguishes them cleanly, 74 Cancelled against 46 Expired.

Non-terminal, so the lead stays enrolled and the next sweep picks them
up when the window passes. A terminal refusal would drop them for ever
for the crime of being early.

off_market_date is a DATE, not a timestamp, so the hold runs from
midnight of the day it came off market. That is what makes John's
example land exactly: cancelled on the 19th, clear any time on the
21st. Both formats in the sheet are handled, ISO and US.

No off_market_date means no evidence of recency, so those are allowed
rather than held. 71 of the 139 MLS leads carry no date, and holding on
a date we do not have would stall them permanently.

THE 90 DAY CONDITION IS NOT IMPLEMENTED, and cannot be from here. John
asked for the hold to apply only where the listing was cancelled inside
90 days on market. The master file has no DOM and no list date: not as
a column (22 columns checked) and not inside Notes (zero matches for
"DOM:" or "List Date:" across all 256 rows). Days on market is simply
not knowable in the Hub today. The hold is therefore applied to every
Cancelled listing, which is the safe direction - a long-DOM
cancellation waits two extra days instead of being texted early - and
the condition is one line to add once DOM reaches the sheet.

The hold is a dial (cx_cancelled_hold_hours, 48, clamped 1-336).

13 tests. The rules-safety guard caught the new entry and made me
record it, which is what it is for.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Conversation Summary card on the lead profile
entries.title: Conversation Summary card on the lead profile
entries.body:
John asked where to see the summary. It was an endpoint only, so the
answer was "you cannot" - this is the card.

It does NOT generate on load. A model call every time somebody opens a
profile is money spent re-reading a thread that has not changed, so the
card shows what is stored and offers a button. When messages have
arrived since it was written it says how many and the button becomes
"Update" rather than presenting stale text as current.

Alongside the paragraph it shows the structured bits the model pulls
out: role, timeline, price expectation, an "In the way" list of
blockers, and the property addresses mentioned. Those are the parts
worth scanning before a call.

Labelled "Written by AI" in the header, always. It sits near the notes
a person typed and must never be mistaken for one.

Placed third in the left column by default, under the pinned Details
and Communications. Anyone with a saved layout gets it appended to
their left column instead, where it can be dragged into place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Auto summary of a lead's conversation, on the profile
entries.title: Auto summary of a lead's conversation, on the profile
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-16. Reading back through forty texts to work out what
somebody said is the slowest part of picking up a lead, and the detail
that matters is buried: an address, a number they have in their head, a
tenant's lease, a spouse who has not been asked yet.

Three rules this obeys, each learned elsewhere in this system:

1. IT CANNOT SEND. There is no send path in the file and none is
   reachable from it. A test greps the source for sendSms,
   sendViaSendGrid, sendSequenceEmail, twilio, scheduleAiAction,
   enrollInDrip and canSendSms and fails if any appears. Summarising is
   a read.
2. IT NEVER TOUCHES . Client notes are one hand-written field
   that must not be machine-stamped. The summary has its own table and
   always reports generated:true so the UI labels it rather than
   passing it off as something a person observed.
3. IT CACHES. GET returns what is stored and says whether it still
   matches the thread; it does NOT generate, so opening a profile never
   costs a model call. POST rebuilds, and only when the conversation
   has actually moved unless forced.

The prompt is seller/buyer aware rather than generic, because what
matters about a real estate lead is the property, the number, the
timing and who else decides. It is told to use only what is in the
transcript, to distinguish what the LEAD said from what WE said, and to
say a thing is unknown rather than infer it. The lead record goes in as
context but marked stale-able: Norma Walker is typed buyer and spent
the whole conversation describing two properties she is selling.

HTML emails are reduced to their subject, so 4KB of table markup never
reaches the model. The transcript is capped at 120 messages, keeping
the most recent.

15 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Expose the rules registry read-only at GET /api/rules
entries.title: Expose the rules registry read-only at GET /api/rules
entries.body:
Read only on purpose. The numbers are safe to change already - rules.js
clamps every one to a range that lives in code - but John should see
the list and confirm the values before anything can write to it. The
edit route lands with the screen, not ahead of it.

It also makes the registry observable, which it was not: with no
endpoint there was no way to confirm from outside whether the deploy
carrying it had actually landed.

Guards are not listed and not reachable from here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Rules registry: the sending dials become editable, inside hard bounds
entries.title: Rules registry: the sending dials become editable, inside hard bounds
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-16: he should be able to review and change these without
asking me. Step one of that is making the numbers safe to change, which
is the part that can hurt somebody. The screen comes next.

server/rules.js holds the 17 numbers that decide when and how often we
contact a person: email caps, the reply hold, texting hours, the text
dedupe gap, AI enrolment limits, Watch thresholds, Home Value limits
and the FSBO day-14 and 30-day cadences.

THE SAFETY MODEL, which is why this is not just a settings table:

  A setting is a DIAL INSIDE A FIXED RANGE, never an override.

Every rule declares hard min/max IN CODE. A stored value outside is
clamped; a missing, blank or unusable one falls back to the default.
No input and no corrupted row can widen a send window past its ceiling
or turn a limit into "unlimited". Failure is always toward LESS
sending: if settings cannot be read at all, every rule returns the
value that is live today.

The guards are deliberately NOT here and cannot be reached from here.
forbidden.js, emailHardBlock and STOP stay in code with tests, because
four fixes failed in that area and a guard you can switch off in a UI
is not a guard. A test asserts no key in the registry even looks like
one.

27 new tests across two files, written before the wiring:

  - the stress test fuzzes all 17 rules with 33 bad inputs each
    (empty, negative, NaN, Infinity, 1e309, hex, unicode digits,
    objects) and asserts the value in force is always inside bounds
  - specific harm cases: texting can never open before 8am or run past
    7pm, caps cannot exceed 1/day and 7/week, the AI limit cannot be
    opened to the whole database, the text gap cannot drop below 15 min
  - the wiring test asserts each call site still produces the number it
    had hardcoded, so introducing the registry changed NOTHING

The stress test earned its place immediately: setRule used a bare
isFinite check, and Number('') and Number([]) are both 0 and both
finite, so submitting a blank field would have been read as zero and
clamped to the minimum - silently moving "texting stops at" from 5pm to
noon. Refused rather than coerced now.

Two stale tests updated, both encoding behaviour John deliberately
changed: hubai's compliance tests did not expect a STOP to also set
Junk (it does, since 10-15, and START deliberately does not undo it),
and the FSBO cadence test still asserted the old 40-47 day gap against
the new 30. Neither was a code defect.

Full suite: no new failures. The 4 remaining assertion failures are
the same ones that predate this work, and the pause_on_reply failure
seen in a full run passes standalone - cross-suite DB pollution, not
this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Past clients get their own Home Value campaign, spaced 3 to 4 weeks
entries.title: Past clients get their own Home Value campaign, spaced 3 to 4 weeks
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-15: "create another version of home value drip for past
clients which we are going to use from now and space these roughly
every 3 to 4 weeks so it feels like a useful periodic update instead of
a sales sequence."

Drip 21 "Home Value — Past Clients", 26 emails, John's past-client copy
verbatim, templates 386-411. Gaps rotate 21/28/24/26 days so it never
reads as clockwork: 615 days end to end, about 20 months.

Same subject, different relationship. The weekly campaign is written
for strangers; this one speaks to someone who already bought or sold
with us.

The spacing also resolves a collision shipped earlier today. Past
clients are capped at one email per 14 days, so putting them in a
WEEKLY campaign would have left most of its sends deferred and arriving
out of order. At 21 to 28 days this sits inside the cap and arrives as
written.

Routing is by status Closed OR a "past client" tag, and falls back to
the weekly campaign if the past-client one is ever missing - a person
with no campaign is worse than one in the wrong campaign.

Two counters had to learn about both campaigns, or this would have
quietly doubled our real sending rate:
  - "already in this campaign" now checks BOTH drips, so somebody in
    the past-client version is not also swept into the weekly one
  - the 300/day quota counts BOTH, because the quota protects the
    sending domain and the domain does not care which drip it was

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: A plain-English opt-out junks them too, not just the STOP keyword
entries.title: A plain-English opt-out junks them too, not just the STOP keyword
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-15: "move both to Junk".

"Take me off your list" and "lose my number" now carry the same
consequence as typing STOP: the status moves to Junk, which pulls them
out of every drip, automation and the AI rather than blocking the text
channel alone. Asking to be left alone in plain English means it just
as much as using the magic word, and leaving those people emailable was
the inconsistency.

This leans on isNaturalOptOut staying conservative, so its guards are
now pinned by a test: "stop by the house", "stop sending me listings in
that range", "I don't check my text messages" and "I don't always
answer texts" must all NOT match. Junking a live lead by mistake costs
a client, so if that pattern is ever loosened the consequence has to be
re-weighed. The activity log records which of the two routes fired.

19 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Group texts: a pool of sending numbers, so one person can be in several
entries.title: Group texts: a pool of sending numbers, so one person can be in several
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-15: "any lead or person should be in any or multiple
group text".

Twilio binds ONE conversation per (participant phone + proxy number)
pair. With a single sending number that is a hard ceiling of one group
per person, and the old code handled the clash by evicting them from
the earlier group - silently, which is the behaviour John hit.

The ceiling is per PROXY, not per account, so each extra number adds
another simultaneous group per person. createGroupText now walks a pool
and picks the first number none of the participants is already bound
to, and refuses with a message naming the fix when they are all taken,
instead of quietly dropping somebody out of an older thread.

Membership is asked of Twilio rather than tracked here, because the
binding lives there: a group ended outside the Hub would make a local
record wrong in the direction that silently drops people.

The pool is the setting twilio_group_proxy_numbers, comma separated,
with the main number always first. Empty setting = one number = exactly
the old behaviour, so nothing changes until numbers are added. Each
added number must join the same A2P campaign or carriers filter it.

Group size was never the limit: 2 to 5 already worked.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Never tell a lead we have spoken when we never have
entries.title: Never tell a lead we have spoken when we never have
entries.body:
John, on Toni Cress: "first text seems to be too blanket."

Her Day 1 was NOT skipped - stage 0 completed and the message carried the introduction
and the site link. What it said was the problem:

  "Hi Toni! It's John with Matt Smith Team at RE/MAX. Just thought I'd check in.
   Has what you're looking for changed at all since we last talked?"

We had never talked. Her record holds ZERO communications of any kind, and the system
knew it - she was enrolled on the COLD_NEVER_CONNECTED lane. She replied STOP
twenty-five minutes later.

12 of the 24 Day 1 openers assume a prior conversation ("since we last talked", "we
connected a while back", "I was looking back at our conversation"). That wording is right
for a dormant lead we really did speak to and wrong for someone who only ever registered
on the site, and nothing chose between them: it was a straight rotation across all 24, so
a stranger had a coin-flip chance of being told we had talked.

handleColdBuyerStage now asks whether a conversation ever actually happened - an inbound
message of any kind, or an outbound text or call. A marketing email they never answered
does not count. A lead we have never spoken to draws only from the 12 openers that make
no such claim; a dormant lead still gets the full bank, because there the reconnect
wording is the right wording.

John's copy is untouched. This selects among his messages, it does not rewrite them. If
filtering ever left nothing, it falls back to the whole bank - a slightly-off message
beats no message.

test/cold-buyer-stranger.test.mjs (10).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: John's rule changes, 2026-10-15
entries.title: John's rule changes, 2026-10-15
entries.body:
Seven changes, each asked for directly.

1. EMAIL REPLY HOLDS A DRIP FOR A MONTH. If a lead emails us, their next
   drip step is pushed to 30 days after that email. Not the same as
   pause_on_reply, which stops a campaign dead: this holds and then
   carries on, so one question in March does not drop someone out of a
   six-month sequence. Measured from THEIR last email, so a second reply
   extends it and nobody has to remember to resume anything. Setting:
   drip_hold_days_after_email_reply.

2. STOP MOVES THEM TO JUNK. A literal STOP now also sets the status,
   which pulls them out of every drip, automation and the AI rather than
   just the text channel. Deliberately NOT applied to the
   natural-language opt-out ("take me off your list"), which still blocks
   texting alone: Junk also stops their email and pushes to FUB, so it is
   kept to the unambiguous case. START un-blocks texting but leaves the
   status for a person.

3. TEXTING RUNS TO 5PM, was 4PM. One exported constant instead of a 16
   repeated in four places, because the same hour decides the greeting
   ("Good afternoon" vs "Hello") and the AI reactivation window, and
   those drifting apart is its own bug.

4. NO KNOWN AREA NOW SENDS THE GENERAL SEARCH rather than no link at all.
   It still does not guess: it drops the area entirely and links
   /property-search/results/, which is accurate for everyone. The openers
   never named the city, so the same wording works.

5. WATCH LEADS ARE SPLIT BY ADDRESS. Watch was refused outright. Now:
   no address + no Hub text in 6 months  -> AI buyer follow-up
   has address + no email from them in 6 months -> Home Value drip
   A Watch lead with an address is a homeowner, not a buyer to chase.

6. FSBO. The 30-day availability check replaces the old 40-47 day
   rotation. And a listing that goes OFF MARKET UNSOLD now gets one
   message, where before the campaign just went quiet - the most useful
   moment we get, wasted. Sent only when fsbo_status is exactly 'Off
   Market' (so not Sold, not Pending) AND there is no mls_status, which
   is what stands in for "listed with an agent" since the FSBO sheet
   carries no such value. Once per lead ever, and the word "FSBO" never
   appears in it - that is our filing term, not what a seller calls
   themselves.

7. PAST CLIENTS: 1 EMAIL IN 14 DAYS. Both Lifelong Friends drips were
   already 30 days apart, so cadence was never the problem - a past
   client sitting in several campaigns was. A cadence cannot see across
   campaigns; a cap can. Counts by status Closed OR a "past client" tag,
   since the two disagree in this data.

18 new tests, 84 existing ones still pass.

entries.subject: A drip stage blocked by a passing condition is postponed, not destroyed
entries.title: A drip stage blocked by a passing condition is postponed, not destroyed
entries.body:
Why Norma Walker's Day 1 never sent. Her schedule says it outright:

  AI_COLD_BUYER  stage=0 (Day 1)  CANCELED
    due    2026-10-12 15:11
    error  US holiday - automated sends paused

Columbus Day was still on the holiday list at 15:11 that afternoon; it was taken off
later the same day. But the holiday was only the trigger. The fault is that the drain
treated "not today" as "never": a blocked stage was CANCELED outright, and the next one
fired three days later as if it had sent. Day 1 is the only message that introduces us
and the only one carrying the site link, so she met us with a Day 4 continuation from a
number she could not place, and replied "Yes. Who is this?".

Worse, quiet hours did not even cancel - logNo returns ok:true, so the stage was marked
COMPLETED. Consumed, never sent, and successful-looking in every report.

Two fixes:

- businessSlot now rolls past US holidays as well as weekends, so a stage is never
  scheduled onto one in the first place. Bumping a holiday can land on a Saturday and
  rolling a weekend can land on a holiday, so both run together until settled.
- The drain distinguishes a block that describes THIS MOMENT (holiday, quiet hours, a
  pause with an end date) from one that describes the LEAD (opted out, DNC, undeliverable,
  a campaign fence, hand-added). The first postpones the stage to the next real sending
  slot keeping its per-lead offset; the second still cancels. Capped at 10 deferrals so a
  permanent condition misread as transient cannot defer forever.

test/cold-buyer-holiday-stages.test.mjs (11). The Columbus Day assertion is deliberately
NOT in there - that date now reads as an ordinary Monday, and asserting otherwise would
be asserting a bug already fixed. Thanksgiving, Christmas and an observed Independence
Day stand in for it.

entries.subject: Introduce ourselves in a lead's FIRST message, whatever stage it is
entries.title: ourselves in a lead's FIRST message, whatever stage it is
entries.body:
John, on Norma Walker: "we did not introduce ourselves and no link."

She was auto-enrolled Monday 2026-10-12 and the first text she ever got was Thursday the
15th - a DAY 4 message. She replied "Yes. Who is this?" and John answered by hand. Two
separate faults put her there.

1. Only 3 of the 24 Day 1 openers actually introduce John. The standing rule is that John
   introduces himself on Day 1 and the thread reads as continuous after that; the copy
   never implemented the first half, so 7 in 8 leads were introduced to nobody and the
   next thing they saw was a question from an unknown number. The site link was fine -
   the renderer appends it on stage 0 - but it only exists on Day 1 too.

2. Day 1 never fired for her at all. The ten stages are pre-scheduled independently at
   enrolment; a blocked or failed one is marked and never retried, while every later
   stage still fires on its own date. So one missed Day 1 silently becomes "no
   introduction, ever" - and her action history shows exactly that: enrolled on the 12th,
   no COLD_BUYER until the 15th, which is stage 2.

The introduction and the site are now tied to being the lead's FIRST message rather than
to the stage number alone: the orchestrator asks whether we have ever sent this lead a
text, and a stage that turns out to be first behaves like Day 1.

John's sentences are NOT rewritten. ensureIntroduction inserts the same sentence the
three complete openers already use, after the greeting, and only when the chosen message
does not already introduce us. Mid-conversation stages are untouched - no
re-introduction, no link - which is what keeps the thread from reading like an
automation.

test/cold-buyer-introduction.test.mjs (13), including her exact message as a first
contact. 61 related AI tests still pass.

entries.title: FUB probe: ask for 'Running', not 'Active' — and name who is mid-plan

was my query being wrong, not a clean result: in FUB, 'Active' is the
status of a PLAN and 'Running' is the status of a PERSON moving
through one. The status totals showed Running=2, so two people are
mid-plan while the per-plan loop said nobody was.

resolves the running people to names/stages/emails so the finding is
actionable. Paused=1516 is reported too: those are people parked
mid-plan who would resume if anyone un-pauses the plan.

entries.subject: Pin a never-contact registration onto the lead once it exists
entries.title: Pin a never-contact registration onto the lead once it exists

The email list already blocks the AI, but it is keyed on the EMAIL: if
anyone later corrects or changes that address the match quietly stops
applying and the AI is free again. A guard that can go silent without
anyone noticing is the failure mode this whole area keeps having.

backfillAiNeverContact() stamps auto_enroll_excluded on any matching
lead that does not have it, on the same 10-minute tick as the fresh
enrolment sweep. That pins the exclusion to the LEAD, where an email
change cannot shake it off, and makes it visible on the profile - which
is what stops somebody switching AI on without realising.

Both layers stay: the email list covers the window before the lead
exists, the stamped flag covers them permanently afterwards.
Idempotent, writes once per lead.

3 more tests (16 total), including one that changes the email after
pinning and asserts the AI is still refused.

entries.subject: AI never-contact list, keyed on email before the lead exists
entries.title: AI never-contact list, keyed on email before the lead exists
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-14: adding Kurt and Lori Johnson (kcoggon2@aol.com) in
Sierra for listing alerts, "make sure that AI doesn't reach out to
them" - said BEFORE the lead exists anywhere in the Hub.

auto_enroll_excluded could not do this: it lives on ai_lead_state and
needs a client_id, so it cannot be set until the Sierra sync has
created the record. In the window between the sync and a person
remembering to tick a box, auto-enrolment runs and the AI can open a
conversation. Closing that window is the whole request, so the
exclusion has to exist before the lead does.

server/ai-never-contact.js registers people by EMAIL and PHONE instead
of id. forbidden.js asks it FIRST, before its own `if (!cid) return
null`, so a record created seconds ago by a sync is already covered.
That is the same choke point canSendSms consults on every AI send -
scheduled, responsive, forced and bulk - which is where the FSBO /
Holly Stock / Megan Walt history says a never-rule has to live. Four
earlier passes failed by guarding whichever door had just broken.

Also closes a real gap found on the way: every never-rule sat behind
canSendSms, and handleFbAdEmail never calls it because it sends EMAIL.
A lead the AI was forbidden to text could still be emailed by it. "AI
doesn't reach out" means any channel the AI speaks on, so forbidden.js
is now asked there too.

Matching is deliberately conservative: last 10 digits for phones so
formatting cannot evade it, case-insensitive email, and placeholder
addresses (notvalidemail) plus sub-10-digit phones never match - two
placeholders are not the same person.

Scoped to the AI channel. These people still get their Sierra listing
alerts, which is why they were added, and nothing here sets a
marketing opt-out - those stay John's to set by hand.

GET/POST /api/ai/never-contact, DELETE /api/ai/never-contact/:id. The
POST also stamps auto_enroll_excluded on any lead that already matches,
so the profile UI and existing audits show it like any other exclusion.

13 tests, including canSendSms with force:true - the exact path that
texted Megan Walt twice. The existing 18-test parity suite still
passes, and an ordinary lead is asserted to be unaffected, since a
guard that quietly silences the AI for everyone is its own outage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Signature on by default in Matt's email composer
entries.title: Signature on by default in Matt's email composer
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-14: "make sure the email signature is default on so he
don't have to keep adding it."

The signature was already saved (and already Matt's details), and /send
and the live preview both append it when a body lacks one. The one
place that did not was the template preview the composer calls - and
picking a template REPLACES the whole body, wiping the signature the
blank composer had put there. So Matt picked a template, saw an
unsigned draft, and typed the signature back in by hand, not knowing
the send would have added it anyway.

Three fixes:

1. /api/email/preview/:templateId/:clientId now appends {{signature}}
   when the template lacks one, using the SAME alreadySigned() guard as
   /send. What the composer shows is now what sends. A template with
   its own hand-built signature block still gets exactly one - that
   guard exists because a lead got two "Matt Smith" blocks on 09-29.

2. The blank composer read the signature out of React state, which
   loses a race against the profile fetch on a fast click after load:
   the composer would open unsigned. It now reads a ref and awaits the
   fetch if it has not landed, so the signature is there either way.
   Same for the Clear-draft button.

3. The savedSignatureHtml() fallback said "RE/MAX Real Estate
   Concepts", which is not the brokerage's name, and omitted the team
   name. Now "Matt Smith Team | RE/MAX Concepts". Only reachable when
   the setting is empty, but wrong is wrong.

Note the signature is ONE team-wide setting, not per-user, so this is
Matt's signature for every login. That matches the convention that
emails go out as Matt. Per-user signatures would be a separate build.

7 tests. Build clean.

entries.subject: Cap every lead at 2 emails a week across all campaigns
entries.title: Cap every lead at 2 emails a week across all campaigns
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-14: "no lead should be getting no more than 2 emails in a
week", applicable to all drip campaigns including active enrollments.

The old rule was 1 campaign email per person per day, counted only from
drip_executions. That misses the real stacking: over the 21 days to
10-14, 138 people went over 2 in a rolling week, worst at 6, from
drip_20 + drip_2 plus the two manual listing sends on 10-10.

server/email-cap.js is now the single place that answers "how many
emails has this person had". It reads email_log, not drip_executions,
because that is the only table that sees every send. Counting:

  - trailing 7 days, rolling, not a calendar week that resets Monday
  - across EVERY campaign and manual send; the inbox does not care
    which part of the Hub sent it
  - matched on client_id OR the same address, since duplicate records
    pointing at one inbox are still one inbox
  - failed sends, bounces and drops excluded; they never arrived

Gated: drips, the FB listing campaign and automation email steps.
Not gated: manual sends (a person deciding to write outranks a queue,
though it still counts) and transactional/first-contact mail, which is
exempt outright and does not consume the budget either - a home value
answer or a new lead's first reply always goes.

A capped send DEFERS, never cancels, so the touch keeps its place.
next_eligible_at is computed from the data (the cap-th newest email
+ 7 days) instead of "retry tomorrow", so a held enrollment does not
re-check daily for a week and fill the activity log.

Enforced at send time, which is what makes it apply to the 4,000+
enrollments that already exist rather than only new ones.

Caps are settings - max_emails_per_week (2) and max_emails_per_day (1)
- tunable without a deploy via POST /api/drips/email-cap/settings.
GET /api/drips/email-cap shows where they sit and who is held.

Dry run over the live log: 220 of 9,693 emails held (2.3%), 136 people,
mostly drip_2 and drip_20. 16 tests. No new failures - the 4 assertion
failures in the suite are identical before and after.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Stop showing AccessTokenExpired over a working call, and watch the Twilio balance
entries.title: Stop showing AccessTokenExpired over a working call, and watch the Twilio balance
entries.body:
Two things John hit on 2026-10-14.

1. Calling Karam Saba showed "AccessTokenExpired (20104)" in red across the call widget
   while the call itself connected fine. A voice token lasts an hour, and the Device
   refreshes it on tokenWillExpire - but that is a background timer, and browsers throttle
   those in a hidden tab, so a tab left open all day holds an expired token and only finds
   out when something uses it. The error was already being handled (it refreshed the token
   and carried on) and ALSO painted across the widget in raw Twilio wording, over a call
   that was working. 20104/31205 now refresh quietly, the same way 31005 already did.

   And the expiry should not be discovered mid-dial at all: the token's age is now tracked,
   anything older than 50 minutes is replaced before the call is placed, and returning to a
   tab that has been hidden tops it up rather than waiting for something to fail. A
   successful refresh also clears the error state, so the phone stops claiming to be broken
   once it is not.

2. "We should be getting an email when balance is becoming low under $5." Twilio does not
   fail loudly when the money runs out - texts stop sending, calls stop connecting, and the
   first sign is a lead who never heard back. server/twilio-balance-alert.js checks hourly
   and emails Matt and John below $5 (threshold and recipients are settings).

   The two ways this goes wrong are both covered: an unknown balance is never treated as
   zero, so an API blip cannot fire a "you are out of money" email; and it sends once on
   the way down and then at most once a day, re-arming as soon as a top-up clears it.
   A blank setting reads as unset rather than as 0 or nobody - a 0 threshold can never be
   met, which is a disabled alert wearing the costume of a working one.

   GET /api/inbox/balance-alert reports what it would do and cannot send.

test/twilio-balance-alert.test.mjs (15).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: AI: auto-pause on any reply, wrong-person doctrine, Day 1 link
entries.title: AI: auto-pause on any reply, wrong-person doctrine, Day 1 link
entries.body:
Three changes from John, 2026-10-13.

1. AUTO-PAUSE ON REPLY. "anyone who responds on AI let's auto pause for now
   until I turn it back on". An inbound reply now cancels the drip (already the
   case) AND stops the AI composing an answer: the lead moves to HUMAN_TAKEOVER
   and a person replies. Gated on ai_auto_pause_on_reply, default '1', so
   turning it back on is a setting and not a deploy. A manual send-now (force)
   still works, so an agent can have the AI draft something deliberately.

2. WRONG PERSON / NOT LOOKING DOCTRINE, in the system prompt for both the buyer
   and cold-seller shapes. If someone says they are not looking, does not
   remember searching, says we have the wrong person, or asks why we contacted
   them: apologize once, acknowledge the information may be outdated, thank
   them, stop. Explicitly banned: arguing, explaining where the data came from,
   ANY mention of website activity or tracking, another qualifying question,
   and "I'll remove you from our list" unless they actually asked. John's two
   examples are included as a tone guide, marked never to be copied verbatim so
   every lead does not get the same sentence.

3. DAY 1 LINK. The site is back on the first text only, as a full tappable
   https URL rather than a bare "MattSmithTeam.com" that many phones leave as
   plain text, and with no "you can browse listings" phrasing. Day 1 is the
   only stage with a website link; the area outreach is the only other link
   anywhere in the sequence.

entries.subject: One profile timeline, newest at the top
entries.title: One profile timeline, newest at the top
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-13: "notes should show from top to bottom newest to oldest."

The lists were grouped by SOURCE, not by date: imported FUB notes, then Sierra's, then
the profile's own free-text notes, each with its own slice and its own Load more button.
So a note from 2016 sat above one typed minutes ago, and on the All tab a brand-new note
landed underneath every email - which is why a note he had just added looked like it had
never saved at all.

Notes, texts, calls, emails and Sierra notes now go into one list ordered newest first,
with one slice and one Load more, so nothing can hide behind a collapsed section.

The two timestamps are not the same kind of thing: a note's stamp is Central WALL TIME
("Oct 13, 2026, 1:23 PM"), a communication's occurred_at is a UTC instant. Both reduce to
the same sortable Central "YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm" string in src/lib/timeline-order.js.
Comparing as strings rather than instants is deliberate - turning a stamp into an instant
needs the correct DST offset for that stamp's own date, and one wrong offset silently
reorders the list, while rendering an instant in Central needs no arithmetic. An
undated note yields no key and sorts to the bottom rather than being given a date nobody
recorded.

Texts, Calls and Emails still exclude notes. Notes stay editable wherever they appear,
through the same NoteRow and handler, so the raw line index still travels with the note.

test/timeline-order.test.mjs (17) covers the keys and the merge, including Patricia
Stuckenschneider's real timeline; test/profile-notes-visible.test.mjs (10) checks the
page is wired to it and that source-grouped rendering has not crept back.

entries.subject: AI buyer nurture: John's rewritten copy, plus area-based value outreach
entries.title: AI buyer nurture: John's rewritten copy, plus area-based value outreach
entries.body:
All 152 messages replaced with John's versions, used verbatim, across Day 1, 4,
9, 17, 30, 50, 80, 120, 165, 210 and the ongoing 45-60 day loop. Copy now lives
in ai-followup/buyer-messages.js so wording can be edited without touching
prompt plumbing.

Three structural changes his rewrite required:

1. Messages are SELF-CONTAINED. Each carries its own greeting and the lead's
   first name. cold-template.js used to bolt "Good afternoon {{first_name}},
   it's John with Matt Smith Team at RE/MAX." onto a bare question, which is
   what made these read like CRM prompts.

2. "You can always browse the latest at MattSmithTeam.com" is GONE from every
   message. It was appended to all of them; the goal of these texts is a reply,
   not a click.

3. John is introduced on Day 1 only. After that the conversation reads as
   continuous rather than reintroduced every time.

AREA-BASED VALUE OUTREACH (ai-followup/area-links.js). On Day 17, Day 30 and the
ongoing loop, a generic message can be replaced by the newest listings for the
community the lead has actually been browsing. Selection order is strongest
signal first: most recent search area, then most-viewed area, then the city on
the lead record. Only the 11 featured communities have pages, and a lead with no
reliable history gets no link and the ordinary message instead - a guessed area
is worse than none. All 11 URLs verified live.

ONE URL PER SMS, enforced in code rather than trusted: the orchestrator counts
URLs and falls back to the plain message if it is ever not exactly one.

Two details worth recording:
- Apostrophes are straight ASCII throughout. A curly apostrophe is outside
  GSM-7 and forces UCS-2, cutting an SMS segment from 160 characters to 70;
  most of these would silently have become 3 segments instead of 1 or 2.
- The greeting is corrected to the send time. The bank mixes "Good morning",
  "Good afternoon" and "Hi", and the rotation has no idea what time it is, so
  "Good morning" at 4pm was inevitable. A mismatched greeting is rewritten,
  "Hi" is left alone, and in the evening a timed greeting becomes "Hi".

24 tests. Longest message is 243 chars, all within 2 segments, none carries a
URL, all greet by name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Inbound-text alerts: Matt on every one, not just after 6 PM

replied to his texts. He was added only when isOffHoursCentral() was true —
weekday after 6 PM Central, any weekend, or a US holiday — so replies during
the working day never reached him.

The time-of-day test is removed outright rather than left as dead code that
looks like it still matters. Both recipient lists now come from settings, so
this never needs another deploy to change:

  inbox_notify_email       main recipient(s), default John
  inbox_notify_always_cc   always copied, default mattsmithremax@gmail.com

A Set still de-duplicates, so an address in both lists is emailed once.

Volume, for the record: inbound texts have run 7-24 a weekday this month and 0
at weekends, so this is roughly 10-20 more emails a day for Matt on a weekday.

entries.subject: Fix: /preview corrupted plain-text bodies by escaping the signature
entries.title: Fix: /preview corrupted plain-text bodies by escaping the signature
entries.body: Shipped a few minutes ago in the /preview rewrite, caught by checking the live endpoint rather than trusting the deploy. The route appended the signature and THEN ran plainToHtml over the whole string. The signature is already HTML, so it came back escaped as visible "<br><div …", and because that escaped text ran straight on from the URL with no whitespace, the link matcher swallowed it into the href: Nested anchors, corrupted URL, no preview card. HTML bodies were unaffected, which is why the composer looked right while the API was mangling plain text. Order is now: plain-to-HTML first, then signature, then merge fields, then the embeds. Two regression tests: one pins the ordering in the route, one asserts no href ever swallows markup and no anchors nest. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)

entries.subject: Link preview card: Dubb layout, sized by aspect, placed with its sentence
entries.title: Link preview card: Dubb layout, sized by aspect, placed with its sentence
entries.body:
Three fixes from John's review of the live result (2026-10-13). 1. SIZE. The card was a fixed 560px wide. Fine for a landscape thumbnail, absurd for a portrait one: Matt's phone videos are 1080x1920, which rendered 996px tall and swamped the email. Both dimensions are now capped (340x300) and the image keeps its aspect, so portrait lands at 169x300 and landscape at 340x153. Width and height are written as attributes because Outlook ignores CSS max-height on images. 2. PLACEMENT. "the video was not positioned next to the actual text" — the card appeared below the signature. The end-of-line test compared the next 40 characters against a whitelist of CLOSING tags, so "

" (the signature block opening) failed it, the link was judged mid-sentence, and its card went to the bottom of the body. It now strips tags up to the next line break and asks whether any visible text remains, which is the real question. 3. LAYOUT, matching Dubb's own card: title above the thumbnail, thumbnail, then a "Watch Video (1:30)" button. The duration comes from the JSON-LD ISO 8601 "duration" on the page, since it is not an OG tag. A non-video page gets "Open link" instead. 32 tests, including the real portrait Dubb video end to end. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)

entries.subject: Email: every link previews, with the image the lead actually receives
entries.title: Email: every link previews, with the image the lead actually receives
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-13: "any link should preview in the email composer in clients",
then "this should apply to any links ... so when leads receive our email it has
image", with a Dubb video link as the example.

Email has no unfurling. Slack and iMessage fetch a page and build a card; no
mail client ever will. So the card has to be built into the HTML before the
message is sent. server/link-preview.js reads Open Graph and builds one.

Dubb needs no special case: it publishes og:image:type image/gif and a GIF with
the play button already drawn on it, so a plain OG reader gets the animated
preview for free. The same path covers Vimeo, Loom, blog posts and anything
else with OG tags. YouTube keeps its existing thumbnail builder because that
needs no network call.

SSRF, since this fetches user-supplied URLs from the server: https only, DNS
resolved and every address checked against private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT
ranges BEFORE connecting, redirects followed manually with the same check each
hop, 8s timeout, 512KB cap, 24h cache. 169.254.169.254 and ::ffff:10.0.0.1 are
both covered by tests.

Placement rule: a URL at the end of its line becomes the card in place (the
video-email shape); a URL mid-sentence stays an inline link and its card is
appended after the body, because a block-level card dropped into a sentence
breaks the sentence. Either way the link previews. One card per unique URL.

Also fixes two things found while checking:
- server/routes/email.js defined POST /preview TWICE. Express matches the
  first, so the second was dead from the day it was added - which is why the
  preview endpoint never applied the YouTube embed despite a comment saying it
  did. The live route now runs the full send pipeline; the duplicate is gone,
  with a test pinning that there is exactly one.
- The Clients composer preview rendered a local approximation. It now asks the
  server for the same HTML the recipient gets, and says so under the frame,
  falling back to the local render if a linked site is slow or down.

24 tests, including against the real Dubb link.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: FSBO: a manual exclusion holds against every automatic path
entries.title: FSBO: a manual exclusion holds against every automatic path
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-12: "make sure nothing gets them enrolled again unless done
manually". Audited all 25 writes to fsbo_followups and closed the three paths
that could have resurrected an excluded lead.

fsboManualDecision() is now the single rule ('removed' or 'paused' = an agent's
choice, cleared only by an agent). Every automatic path asks it instead of
re-deriving the rule in its own SQL.

Three guards on the auto-enroll sweep, not one:
  1. the candidate query (already there)
  2. an explicit check by client id, so a future edit to that JOIN cannot
     re-open the door
  3. a WHERE on the upsert itself. Without it, INSERT..ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE
     SET status='active' would flip a 'removed' row straight back to active —
     the one statement in the system that could undo an exclusion. An
     OFF_MARKET 'stopped' row can still revive, which is the intended re-entry
     path for a relisted FSBO.

Two more paths closed:
- /api/lists/fsbo/followup/seed inserts status='active' outright. It now skips
  leads carrying a manual decision and reports them as skipped.
- MERGE. doMerge copies fsbo_status onto the survivor when the survivor has
  none, so folding an excluded FSBO record into a plain lead moved the FSBO
  identity to a record with no decision row, and the sweep would enroll it. The
  decision belongs to the person, so carryFsboDecisionToSurvivor() moves it.
  An exclusion wins over the survivor's active campaign (an agent saying "do
  not text this seller" should stop the texting, and it is one click to undo),
  but never overrides a decision the survivor already made, and never clears
  attempt_count or enrolled_at.

22 tests, one per path, all executing the real statements. Full suite shows no
new failures: its failing set varies run to run from pre-existing cross-suite
DB pollution, and a name-level diff against a stashed baseline is empty.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: FSBO campaign: let an agent exclude a lead before enrolment
entries.title: FSBO campaign: let an agent exclude a lead before enrolment
entries.body:
A FSBO below the DOM-14 threshold has no fsbo_followups row, so pause and
remove were UPDATEs that matched nothing and still returned ok. The lead then
auto-enrolled the day they crossed the threshold, with no way to stop it from
the profile (John, 2026-10-12, on Deborah Emrich at DOM 3).

- pause/remove now upsert a decision row. The evaluator already treats
  'removed'/'paused' as excluded, and the auto-enroll sweep only picks up leads
  with no row or an OFF_MARKET stop, so the decision holds at DOM 14 and later.
- enrolled_at stays NULL on a pre-enrolment row, which is how an undo tells the
  two cases apart.
- allowBackIntoFsboCampaign deletes a pre-enrolment decision instead of
  reactivating it: resume demands current eligibility, and a DOM-3 lead is
  'waiting', so reactivating would refuse. Deleting returns them to the clean
  un-decided state the sweep looks for. resume routes there automatically, so
  one button covers both cases. An enrolled row is never deleted.
- profile: "Exclude from campaign" and "Hold" on a waiting/eligible lead,
  "Allow back in" on a removed one, and a line saying a lead excluded before
  enrolment was never texted.

Tests execute the real SQL against the real schema rather than reading source,
which is what let the UPDATE-with-no-row bug ship.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Blast list is all 66: NO_MARKETING is an imported tag, not an opt-out
entries.title: Blast list is all 66: NO_MARKETING is an imported tag, not an opt-out
entries.body:
I excluded ten past clients because their Hub record carried NO_MARKETING. John
asked where that tag comes from, and the answer makes the exclusion wrong:

  - nothing in this codebase creates it
  - nothing in this codebase honours it. emailHardBlock checks email_status and
    isBlockedEmail; a real opt-out is marketing_email_opt_out or
    email_status='OptedOut'
  - it arrived in the 2026-05-11 bulk import, alongside Import, Imported Stage:,
    Fello, Dealmachine, Database REfresh
  - it is ALWAYS paired with NO_TEXT, which is a vendor export's two columns, not
    ten individual decisions
  - it is on thousands of records

The source CSV had already judged this correctly: the tag sits in SoftNotes,
described as a bulk import tag, while OptOutFlags - the column for real opt-outs,
which put 25 other rows on DO NOT BLAST - was empty for all ten. I treated a
decorative tag as authoritative over the file's own explicit classification.

The list now filters what actually blocks a send: marketing_email_opt_out, and
email_status in OptedOut / ReportedAsSpam / WrongAddress. All ten were re-checked
against those fields before being added - all clear, nine ValidAddress and one
TwoWayEmailing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Past-client blast list as a tag-driven smart list
entries.title: Past-client blast list as a tag-driven smart list
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-09: put the weekly email in templates with a first-name merge field,
and make the READY rows of past-clients-sierra-blast-ready-2026-10-09.csv a list.

Of 66 READY rows, all 66 matched a Hub client by email. 56 are clean. 10 carry a
NO_MARKETING tag and are EXCLUDED: the CSV's own notes call that tag a bulk-import
artifact, which may well be true, but overriding an opt-out marker is a human
decision and not mine to make quietly. They are named in the reply so John can
decide.

Tag-driven rather than a frozen set of ids, so adding or removing someone is a tag
edit and the list follows. The query also re-checks NO_MARKETING at read time, so
if that tag is ever applied to someone on the list they drop out without anyone
having to remember to update it.

Tagging was read-modify-write: tags is a JSON array and writing it blind would
have wiped every other tag on 56 past-client records.

Template 384 carries the HTML with "Hi friends," replaced by "Hi {{first_name}},".
That merge field falls back to "there", so a blank name reads "Hi there," rather
than "Hi ,".

entries.subject: Precompute the condo-band flag: 6.99s per page load was the viewers list
entries.title: Precompute the condo-band flag: 6.99s per page load was the viewers list
entries.body:
With per-list timing in place the answer was unambiguous: marion_condo_viewers
took 6.99s of an 8.0s /api/clients/smart-lists, which the Clients page calls on
every load. My earlier index-and-split-the-OR fix moved it 9.4s -> 8.2s, because
the real costs were the price CAST, lower(city) and lower(trim(address)) — none
of which can use an index however the joins are arranged.

So it is computed once and read instantly: fub_activity.marion_condo_band, with
an index on (client_id, marion_condo_band). The smart list is now a single
indexed EXISTS.

POST /api/admin/refresh-condo-band recomputes it after a condo import or a large
activity sync.

The lesson is the measurement, not the fix: I assumed my lists were the cause,
"fixed" them, saw 8.2s and only then added timing. Adding the timing first would
have cost one deploy instead of three.

entries.subject: The Marion smart lists made every Clients page load take 9.4s
entries.title: The Marion smart lists made every Clients page load take 9.4s
entries.body:
John asked why the Hub felt slow today. It was me. /api/clients/smart-lists —
which the Clients page calls on every load — went to 9.4 seconds, while the API
itself was still answering in 0.3s. Measuring the endpoints one by one is what
found it; "the Hub is slow" would have been guesswork.

Two causes, both in the smart lists I added today:

The viewer query joined fub_activity to condo_properties on `mls_number = prop_mls
OR address = prop_street`. An OR across two different columns cannot use either
index, so it full-scanned 38,195 view rows for each of 46,000 clients. It is two
separate EXISTS now, each able to use an index.

And there were no indexes to use anyway: fub_activity had one on client_id and
nothing on prop_mls or prop_street. Both added.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Marion condos as SMART lists, not saved lists
entries.title: Marion condos as SMART lists, not saved lists
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-08: "it should be on smart list not saved list".

He is right, and the difference matters: a saved list is a frozen set of ids that
is wrong the next time someone views a condo or an address is corrected. A smart
list is live SQL, so it is always current.

  marion_condo_viewers  viewed a Marion condo $150k-$300k, ever, confirmed
                        against the MLS export by MLS# or address
  marion_condo_owners   lives at an address that IS a Marion condo — sellers

Both exclude dead, DNC, archived and STOP, like every prospecting list here.

The owner match needed a decision. Replicating the JS address normalisation in
raw SQL would have meant a pile of REPLACE() calls that silently drift from the
real one, so clients.address_key stores the SAME addressKey() output the condo
import uses, and the smart list is an exact join on it. The clients PUT keeps it
in step when an address is edited, and POST /api/admin/refresh-address-keys
backfills, since 45,000 rows predate the column.

prop_price is free text, so the price band compares digits rather than a string.

Both queries were EXECUTED against the real schema before committing, not just
read — the habit that was missing when the MLS join silently never landed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Who OWNS a Marion condo, from the same MLS export
entries.title: Who OWNS a Marion condo, from the same MLS export
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-08: "also this would be a good data for those that owns a condo in
Marion". A lead whose own address is a condo in the export is a potential SELLER
— a different list from the people browsing them, and often a better one.

GET /api/admin/condo-owners?city=Marion matches a client's address against the
1,396 condos, normalising street type and directionals first, because the Hub
writes "3900 Deer Valley Dr" where the MLS writes "3900 Deer Valley Drive B".
The match reuses addressKey rather than reimplementing the same rules in SQL and
letting the two drift apart.

Each result carries the MLS record — subtype, last sale price and date, year
built, beds and baths — so the lead can be approached with something real.

Dead, DNC, archived and STOP excluded, like every prospecting list here. The
response says plainly that a match means the lead LIVES at a known condo
address, which is evidence of ownership and not proof of it.

entries.subject: The MLS condo join was never actually in the file
entries.title: The MLS condo join was never actually in the file
entries.body:
The rebuilt list grew 147 -> 183 but reported ZERO matches from the MLS export,
while a direct check showed 215 overlapping MLS numbers. The join worked; it just
was not there.

The script that was meant to add the join, the condo_mls select and the MLS
signal asserted on its LAST edit and aborted — so it wrote none of the three. I
added the fourth edit separately, saw it land, and took that as the whole change
having applied. Every subsequent result was produced by text patterns alone and
looked plausible enough not to question.

All three are in now, verified by grepping for each one individually rather than
trusting the script's exit, and the query is executed against the real schema.

The join also matches on address as well as MLS#, since 209 Marion views match
the export by address — a view that arrived without an MLS number is still a
condo.

entries.subject: Condo identification stops guessing: import the MLS export
entries.title: Condo identification stops guessing: import the MLS export
entries.body:
John supplied an Agent Single Line export — 1,396 Marion condos, every row
SubType CON/ZER/CO-OP, 1,380 sold / 10 pending / 7 active, MLS# and address on
every one.

This is the only authoritative statement of what IS a condo anywhere in the
system. FUB's property object HAS a `type` field and it comes through empty on
this account, along with bedrooms, bathrooms and area; listings.property_type is
unpopulated too. Until now the Marion list rested entirely on the word "condo"
appearing in listing text, which is why it showed no condo views after Oct 2025
while Marion itself had 354 views this year.

condo_properties is keyed on MLS#, which joins straight to fub_activity.prop_mls,
and on a normalised address so an OWNER can be matched as well as a viewer.
Re-importing refreshes rather than duplicating.

The MLS match is now the first signal checked, and it names the MLS number and
subtype in the result. The text signals stay as fallbacks for properties the
export does not cover, and each still says which one fired — a guess must never
read like a fact.

Also added the pattern this feed actually uses for units: a BARE TRAILING LETTER,
"3900 Deer Valley Drive B". 18 of 687 Marion addresses are written that way and
the Unit/Apt/# patterns matched none of them.

entries.subject: property-interest joined a column realist_properties does not have
entries.title: property-interest joined a column realist_properties does not have
entries.body:
The endpoint 500'd on its first real call: "no such column: r.mls_number".
realist_properties is keyed on the ADDRESS, not an MLS number — I assumed the
column and never ran the query.

This is the same mistake as `active` on drip_campaigns, two days of work apart,
and I had already written the test that catches it. I just did not point it at
this file. Now I have: the property-interest SELECT is extracted and EXECUTED
against the real schema, and a second test asserts realist is joined on the
address — and fails loudly if realist ever gains an MLS column, so the join gets
revisited rather than silently staying second-best.

Reading a query proves it was written. Running it proves it works.

entries.subject: Save a property-interest search as a named client list
entries.title: Save a property-interest search as a named client list

with the same name — a duplicate "Marion Condo Campaign" is worse than no list,
because someone will work the stale one.

entries.subject: Prospecting results never include dead, DNC or a STOP
entries.title: Prospecting results never include dead, DNC or a STOP
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-08: "all active status only correct no dead or dnc".

junk, donotcontact and archived are excluded ALWAYS, not on request, along with
anyone who replied STOP. A lead-mining list that quietly includes people we may
not contact is a trap — the whole point of the list is that someone will act on
it. `status=` narrows to exactly one status when that is wanted, and the response
reports the status breakdown so the mix is visible rather than assumed.

Also fixed a test of my own making: it located the text-delivery breakdown with a
bare indexOf('by_status:'), and this endpoint now has a by_status key earlier in
the file, so it was checking the wrong query. It scopes to the route first. That
is the third time an unanchored indexOf has pointed a test at the wrong thing in
this file.

entries.subject: Read-only: who looked at what, by city, price and type
entries.title: Read-only: who looked at what, by city, price and type
entries.body:
John, 2026-10-08: "who looked at condos in Marion in the $150k-$300k price range
in the last few years, even if it's just 1 view".

GET /api/admin/property-interest?city=&min=&max=&since=&type=condo groups
fub_activity by lead and reports the views behind each one.

Two things it is careful about:

prop_price is free text — "$225,000", "225000", "$1.2M" — so it parses digits and
honours a k/M suffix rather than trusting a string compare.

NO TABLE RECORDS A PROPERTY TYPE, so "condo" is inferred, and the endpoint says
which signal matched on every property: the listing's own property_type or
Realist building_type where the MLS number joins, the word condo in the listing,
or a unit number in the address. A judgement call stays visible on each row
instead of disappearing into a total.

debug=1 returns the shape of the data — row counts, top cities, price samples,
the property types that actually exist — because guessing at the distribution is
how you build a filter that silently matches nothing and call it an answer.

entries.subject: Raise the per-lead bound to 150s; 90s was cutting off slow-but-finishing leads
entries.title: Raise the per-lead bound to 150s; 90s was cutting off slow-but-finishing leads
entries.body:
Six leads errored in the first 25 batches. Timing one without the bound showed
what they are: travis.suhr@gmail.com took 97 seconds and found 81 messages, of
which 71 were already in the Hub and 10 were listing alerts — 0 new.

So they are not huge mailboxes. The IMAP search across the team mailboxes is just
slow regardless of how much it finds, and 90s sat right on top of that. 150s
clears it while still bounding the batch.

The timeout message now prints the actual bound instead of a hardcoded "90s" that
would have quietly lied the moment the value changed — which it just did.

The driver's own request timeout goes to 360s to stay above two leads at the new
bound; a client timeout firing before the server's defeats the whole point of
moving the bound server-side.

entries.subject: Bound each lead inside the sweep, so one big mailbox cannot stall it
entries.title: Bound each lead inside the sweep, so one big mailbox cannot stall it
entries.body:
A lead out-ran the client's 240s timeout. When the request dies the caller gets
nothing back — not even how far it got — so the cursor cannot advance and the
same lead is retried forever. The client-side "step past a stuck lead" guard only
advances the cursor by one id, which does not reliably clear a slow lead when ids
are sparse: it could take hours of 8-minute double-timeouts to get past one
person.

The fix belongs on the server. Each lead now runs under a 90s race, so the batch
always returns, last_id moves past the slow lead, and that lead is reported as an
error instead of stalling the sweep.

3 tests, including that last_id is set BEFORE the lead is attempted — otherwise a
failure would leave the cursor behind and reintroduce the same loop.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: The push was chasing a target the Gmail import kept growing
entries.title: The push was chasing a target the Gmail import kept growing
entries.body:
Caught by watching the live run rather than the log's success lines: `remaining`
went 1397 -> 1429 -> 1409 -> 1396 while 20 rows a batch were being written. A
finite job does not behave like that.

Two faults, both mine.

gmail_ ROWS WERE TREATED AS HUB-ORIGINATED. They are not — a gmail_ row is email
the Hub IMPORTED out of the team mailboxes. Pushing it to FUB sends mail back
toward the system it came from, as a note, and the Gmail sweep running alongside
creates more of them continuously. So the push had no end: every email imported
became another row to push. Only twilio_ and hub_ are eligible now, which is what
"Hub-originated" was supposed to mean all along.

THE REMAINING COUNT IGNORED `since`. The batch query filtered on occurred_at and
the count did not, so the driver could never see `done` and the number reported
work that would never be done. It takes the same filter now.

580 notes were written before I stopped it. They are real Hub texts and calls from
October — the `since` filter kept the historical Gmail imports out of the batch
even while they inflated the count — so nothing wrong landed in FUB, and
fub_comm_pushed means a re-run will not duplicate them.

23 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Sweep the leads whose email history is actually worth recovering first
entries.title: Sweep the leads whose email history is actually worth recovering first
entries.body:
The first real run made the ordering problem obvious. 45,000 leads at roughly six
seconds each is about 75 hours, and by client id the oldest records come first —
long-standing clients whose mail the inbox poller already has. Lead 4 is the shape
of it: 52 messages found, 29 dropped as listing alerts, 23 kept, and all 23
already in the Hub. Correct behaviour, hours of work, nothing gained.

`statuses` narrows the sweep, so closed / pending / active can run first — a few
thousand leads rather than forty-five thousand — and the remaining count respects
the same filter instead of reporting the whole table.

POST /api/inbox/email-history/bulk {statuses: ["closed","pending","active"]}

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: The importer no longer re-adds the texts we just deleted
entries.title: The importer no longer re-adds the texts we just deleted
entries.body:
Caught by an import dry run while verifying the push: it reported it would add 7
texts for a lead, which means the very next conversation import brings all 17,204
bodyless rows straight back and silently undoes the cleanup John asked for.

A text FUB will not give us the words for is not worth a row, so the importer now
drops it on the way in and reports skipped_no_body. The deletion and the import
rule now agree, which is the only way a purge stays purged.

Texts only. A NOTE containing that phrase is still a real note worth keeping, and
a test pins that distinction.

entries.subject: Two things the first dry run exposed before anything was written
entries.title: Two things the first dry run exposed before anything was written
entries.body:
Dry-running the push against live data, rather than trusting the tests, showed
what would actually have landed in FUB.

RAW HTML. Hub email bodies are HTML, so the note read
"[Hub] Email ... | <div style="font-family:Arial,He" with the real sentence
buried somewhere inside. It now goes through the same htmlToText the import side
already uses, so both directions read the same. Plain text is left untouched; the
stripper only runs when the body actually looks like HTML.

THE HUB TALKING TO ITSELF. The first three eligible rows were internal mail on
Matt's own client record — a TC Morning Update, a home-value request alert, a
"Krisstie Speth emailed you" notification — all addressed to FUB person 6456.
Those records exist so internal mail has somewhere to land; they are not
conversations with a lead. Team addresses are excluded now, in the batch query
and in the remaining count, which otherwise would have reported work that would
never be done.

4 more tests. 19 total.
