entries.subject: Bounces now stop the email, and say why
entries.title: Bounces now stop the email, and say why
entries.body:
The loop that was missing. A bounce was recorded and nothing acted on it: 86 addresses
SendGrid had already rejected were still marked sendable, 25 were still enrolled in live
campaigns, and 61 sends were discarded before they left the building.

THE SMTP CODE DECIDES, NOT A RETRY COUNT. Half the bounces on file are recoverable, so a
blanket "three strikes" would be wrong in both directions: it hammers dead mailboxes two
extra times each, and risks dropping real people whose inbox happened to be full that week.

  permanent   550 5.1.1 no such mailbox     stopped on the FIRST failure
  temporary   inbox full, inactive, 4.x.x   kept; stopped after 3 failures over 30+ days
  spam        the person pressed report      stopped immediately, opt-out flag set

The trap worth naming: Gmail and Outlook answer "inbox full" with a FIVE-series code
(5.2.2). Reading the first digit alone would have thrown away real people - Nicole Long
among them, whose address is fine and who simply has a full inbox.

EVERY STOP SAYS WHY. A tag on the lead (filterable in the Clients list), a note on the
profile carrying the actual SMTP response rather than a summary, and an activity row:

  Email Stopped: Hard Bounce
  Email Stopped: Spam Report
  Email Stopped: Repeated Soft Bounce

Stopping also ends any active drip enrolment, so a suppressed address stops consuming
campaign slots.

POST /api/email/backfill-bounces applies the same policy to everything that already failed,
using SendGrid's own suppression lists as the source of truth - the Hub never recorded why
anything bounced, so its own log cannot answer the question. Takes {dry:true}.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Email: record WHY a message failed, and read SendGrid's own suppression lists
entries.title: Email: record WHY a message failed, and read SendGrid's own suppression lists
entries.body:
John asked whether to retry a bounce a few times before giving up, or whether we already
know which addresses are genuinely dead. We did not know. The Hub recorded that an email
bounced and nothing else, so a dead mailbox and a full one looked identical and no retry
policy was possible at all.

SendGrid sends the answer on every bounce and it was being thrown away:
  type    'bounce' = the server rejected it, 'blocked' = reputation or throttling
  reason  the SMTP response, e.g. "550 5.1.1 ... does not exist"
  status  5.x.x permanent, 4.x.x temporary

email_events now keeps all three. Going forward every failure is classifiable.

For the 156 bounces already on record, GET /api/email/suppressions reads SendGrid's own
lists, which is ground truth rather than inference. It keeps the four apart because they
mean different things and deserve different handling:

  bounces  rejected by the server; 5.x.x permanent, 4.x.x worth retrying
  blocks   reputation or throttling; usually temporary
  invalid  malformed, or a domain that does not resolve; never deliverable
  spam     the person pressed report spam; permanent, and a compliance matter

Read-only. It neither modifies SendGrid state nor writes to the Hub - a test asserts both,
because a suppression endpoint that can delete suppressions is a foot-gun.

No suppression policy is applied yet. That needs the classification above to exist first,
and it needs John's decision on the retry threshold.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Type: the stylesheet was two steps behind the JSX
entries.title: Type: the stylesheet was two steps behind the JSX
entries.body:
Client Details read visibly smaller than Communications on the client profile, and the
reason is that this app has TWO type systems. Communications is styled with inline
fontSize and got scaled twice. Client Details is styled by .cp-* rules in app.css, which
got scaled neither time - 274 hardcoded font-size declarations, 125 of them at 12px.

app.css now replays both passes in order rather than guessing one multiplier, so it lands
on exactly the values the JSX already has:

    pass 1   11->12  12->13  12.5->13  13->14  13.5->14
    pass 2   x1.10 to the nearest half pixel

    12px -> 14.5      13px -> 15.5      14px -> 15.5      16px -> 17.5

Three rules survived the sweep and were fixed by hand rather than by re-running the
catch-up, because that script is not idempotent and a second pass would have double-scaled
the other 271.

scale-type.mjs now rewrites hardcoded font-size as well as the tokens, so the two systems
cannot drift apart on the next change. Three tests pin it: no rule may sit at a pre-scale
size, the scaler must touch both, and Client Details rows must not fall behind 15px.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Type: +10% across the whole Hub
entries.title: Type: +10% across the whole Hub
entries.body:
John asked for 10% on top of the FUB-matched sizes. Both layers had to move: the tokens in
app.css, and the 1,227 inline fontSize declarations in the JSX that actually govern what is
on screen.

     783   13   -> 14.5
     351   14   -> 15.5
      22   18   -> 20
      11   16   -> 17.5
      10   17   -> 18.5
     ...   plus the six --text-* tokens

Sizes land on the nearest HALF pixel rather than a whole one. Rounding 13px up to a whole
14 is 8.3%, not 10, and at the sizes this app uses the rounding error is most of the
adjustment. The actual average increase is 11.2%.

Anything under 9px is left alone - at that size the text is an icon-adjacent label and
scaling it does more harm than good.

The codemod is kept at scripts/scale-type.mjs and takes --scale, so a further step is one
command. It is deliberately NOT idempotent: running it twice compounds, which makes "one
more step" a decision rather than something that happens by accident.

Two typography tests asserted the sizes matched FUB exactly. That stopped being the intent
the moment 10% was asked for on top, so they now assert the floor and the hierarchy instead
of fixed numbers - which is what actually matters and what will survive the next change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Type: raise the inline sizes, because the tokens were not controlling them
entries.title: Type: raise the inline sizes, because the tokens were not controlling them
entries.body:
Matching the tokens to FUB barely changed anything on screen, and the live page showed why:
1,228 inline `fontSize` declarations across the JSX beat any stylesheet rule, and the app's
dominant size was 12px (661 uses), not the 14px token. The Clients list is not even a
table - it is divs - so the table rules reached almost nothing.

One step up, applied to 1,103 sites across 41 files:

     661   12px -> 13px
     301   13px -> 14px
     122   12.5px -> 13px
      13   13.5px -> 14px
       6   11px -> 12px

Anything already 14px or larger is untouched. Those are headings and deliberate emphasis;
moving them would change the hierarchy rather than the legibility, and the ask was
legibility.

The codemod is kept at scripts/bump-inline-type.mjs. It only rewrites a NUMERIC fontSize
inside a style object, so string values like '0.9em' are left alone - those are relative
already and scale on their own.

The real lesson is that this app cannot be restyled from app.css alone. 1,228 inline sizes
is the actual design system, and the tokens are decoration until that is reversed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Deploys stop taking the Hub down, and typography matched to Follow Up Boss
entries.title: Deploys stop taking the Hub down, and typography matched to Follow Up Boss
entries.body:
TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS, ONE OF WHICH WAS NOT WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE.

1. "The site becomes unavailable for a few minutes, then we have to hard refresh."

   The cause was not slow booting. fetch() only REJECTS on a network failure, never on an
   HTTP error, so while Render swapped instances its 502 page came back as a perfectly
   good Response. The service worker's catch block never ran, the cached shell was never
   used, and the error page went straight to the user - for the whole restart.

   A non-OK response is now treated exactly like being offline: an open tab keeps working
   on the version it already has, using assets it already cached, until the new instance
   is reachable. A failed asset fetch also gets one retry after 1.2s, because a single
   missed chunk white-screens a tab until a hard refresh.

   The update check moved from hourly to every 2 minutes AND on tab focus. Hourly meant a
   tab left open during a deploy could sit on the old bundle for up to an hour and then
   pick up the new one at an arbitrary moment.

2. Typography matched to FUB.

   FUB sets proxima-nova, which is licensed through Adobe Fonts - it cannot be self-hosted
   or pulled from Google Fonts. Figtree is the closest free face: same geometric-humanist
   build and open apertures, and it holds at 13-14px where Montserrat is too wide and
   Inter reads colder. The stack already names Proxima Nova, so buying the licence later
   is a Typekit link plus one token.

   Matched exactly: 16px sections, 14px body AND TABLE ROWS (13px was the main thing
   making dense screens hard to read), and FUB's softer text colours - rgb(54,70,80) for
   body, rgb(147,165,178) for secondary, rather than near-black.

   ONE DELIBERATE DEPARTURE: FUB sets 14px text on a 14px line. That is fine for a
   single-line cell and hard work the moment anything wraps. The ask was readability, so
   single-line cells stay compact and anything that can wrap gets real leading. Copying
   1.0 everywhere would have worked against the point of the request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Dashboard: lifetime totals in one read
entries.title: Dashboard: lifetime totals in one read
entries.body:
"How many texts have we received" had no answer anywhere. The dashboard counted outgoing
only, /api/email/stats counted the send log, and the inbox list caps at 1000 rows with no
count at all.

GET /api/dashboard/totals returns email, text and call volume in both directions, AI
enrolment, drip reach and client counts. It reads counts and nothing else.

Two distinctions the numbers would otherwise hide:

  email_log vs communications - the first is what the Hub actually SENT through SendGrid,
  the second is the conversation record, which also holds email history imported from
  Gmail. Both are reported, because using either one alone answers a different question
  than the one being asked.

  enrolments vs people - one person can sit in more than one campaign, so counting
  enrolments overstates how many people are being emailed. Both are reported.

AI "enrolled" is managed AND enabled. A lead handed to a human can stay flagged as managed,
so the managed count alone overstates it; both are returned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value intake: run the poller, and tell the team a request came in
entries.title: Home Value intake: run the poller, and tell the team a request came in
entries.body:
Nicole Morris submitted a home value request at 5 PM on 2026-09-29. She got no follow-up
email, and John never heard about it. Two causes, neither of them the matching logic.

1. pollHomeValueSubmissions existed, worked, and nothing ever called it. The only way to
   process a submission was a manual POST to /home-value/intake, so requests sat in the
   mailbox until somebody thought to run it. Now on a 10-minute interval, with its own
   catch so a failing IMAP poll cannot take the scheduler down with it.

2. The Sierra notification only reaches mattsmithremax@gmail.com. A request could be
   received, matched and answered without John seeing any of it. The intake now emails
   both of them when a submission lands, deduped through activity_log the same way the FB
   lead alert is, so re-reading the mailbox cannot alert twice for one form.

The alert also names BOTH names when they differ. She submitted as "Nicole Morris" and
matched the existing record for "Niki Morris" on her email address - correctly, and with
no duplicate created - but seeing one name in the form and another in the Hub is exactly
what makes somebody think the system made a mess.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value: warm up to 200/day instead of starting there
entries.title: Home Value: warm up to 200/day instead of starting there
entries.body:
200 cold emails a day from one sending domain is a real step up in volume, and mailbox
providers judge a sender on how suddenly that volume appears. Five enrolment days at 50,
five at 100, then the configured ceiling.

It counts DAYS THAT ACTUALLY ENROLLED rather than calendar days, so a weekend, a holiday
or an outage cannot quietly spend a step of the ramp while sending nothing. Today does not
count itself either, so a morning run cannot raise its own afternoon limit. Nobody has to
remember to raise the number, and the ceiling still wins if it is set lower than a ramp
step.

The settings endpoint now echoes excluded_ids, ramp_day and todays_limit back. The
exclusion list was write-only: the one setting that keeps named people out of the campaign
could not be read to confirm it had saved, which had to be proved by adding a known-
eligible person and watching the eligible count fall by one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value enrollment: actually run it
entries.title: Home Value enrollment: actually run it
entries.body:
The engine had a daily limit, an on/off setting and an exclusion list, and nothing ever
called it. Turning enrollment "on" did nothing whatsoever - the only way anyone was ever
enrolled was a manual POST to /home-value/run. `home_value_enroll_enabled` now means
something.

Weekday mornings at 9 AM CT. The hour matters: a day's batch is scheduled across the 9-5
send window, so 200 leads trickle out over eight hours. Enrolling late in the day would
compress the same volume into the last hour, which is the wrong shape for a cold list.
Weekdays only, because this is prospecting.

The day is claimed in app_settings BEFORE the tick runs, so a slow run cannot double-enroll,
matching the FSBO and Watch sweeps.

chicagoNow() gained a `weekday`. It had none, so the weekend check read `undefined === 0`
-- false -- and would have enrolled every Saturday. It is derived from the Chicago calendar
date at noon UTC, because 10 PM CT Friday is already Saturday in UTC and reading the UTC
day would skip a Friday and permit a Saturday.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Email: the home value auto-response had no unsubscribe, and signed itself twice
entries.title: Email: the home value auto-response had no unsubscribe, and signed itself twice
entries.body:
Found by reading a delivered message in Matt's mailbox rather than the code, after John
asked whether the home value email carries an unsubscribe. It does not, and the reason
was three separate gaps:

1. The intake sends under the category `home_value_followup`, which did not match the
   `<prefix>_<id>` bulk pattern, so no opt-out was attached at all. It answers something
   the person asked for, but it also invites further contact ("Someone from the Matt
   Smith Team may reach out"), which is what makes it marketing rather than purely
   transactional. Added to the gate by name.

2. /api/email/send accepted a `category` in the request body and never passed it to
   sendViaSendGrid, so a send explicitly marked as marketing silently got no footer
   either, and the caller had no way to tell. A 1:1 email still passes nothing and still
   gets no footer, which is correct - the difference is that asking now works.

3. The composer appended Matt's saved signature to a template that already ended in one.
   Its comment claimed it skipped "a literal signature already typed"; the code only ever
   checked for the {{signature}} token. A real lead received the follow-up with two
   "Matt Smith" blocks and two phone numbers. alreadySigned() now looks for the
   signature's own details - phone, email, domain, brokerage line - and takes TWO of them,
   so a body that merely mentions the office number once is not mistaken for a signed one.
   The live preview uses the same rule, so what it shows is what sends.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Names: tidy them at ingest too, so the file stops drifting back
entries.title: Names: tidy them at ingest too, so the file stops drifting back
entries.body:
The bulk repair left "Zinse FADONOUGBO" still shouting. Two separate causes, both now
closed.

The first was the paging bug fixed in 55a854b: walking the file under a non-unique sort
skipped a handful of rows. Re-run under id_asc, the whole file needed only 14 more
records - 3 the walk had missed, plus these:
  - "W Patrick W" -> "W Patrick"   an initial before the name AND a duplicate after it;
    safe to drop here because two tokens remain, which is why the main pass's guard
    against reducing "B J" to "B" did not apply
  - "Charles H & Lori A" -> "Charles & Lori"   both middle initials, or the pair reads
    inconsistently
  - last_name holding nothing but "And"  ->  empty
  - " Parceros " -> "Parceros"   an entity keeps its spelling, but not its stray spaces

The second is that Sierra hands names back as they were typed upstream, so every sync
re-imports ALL CAPS surnames and "Mcgowan". processLead now runs the same tidyName pass
the email merge uses, which is what makes this stay fixed rather than needing another
sweep next month. It only title-cases a value that is entirely one case, so "ShaLynn"
and "DeWitt" are untouched, and Mac names stay as spelled.

Verified across all 45,878 clients under stable paging: 0 ALL CAPS surnames, 0 stray
whitespace, 0 doubled spaces, 0 uncapitalised Mc/O' names outside junk records. The
address audits re-run clean too - 0 in every class, and 23,581 of 23,679 addresses
render exactly as stored.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Clients list: a unique sort key, because paging the whole file was unreliable
entries.title: Clients list: a unique sort key, because paging the whole file was unreliable
entries.body:
A re-audit after the name repair still showed an ALL CAPS surname, "Zinse FADONOUGBO".
The record was not new (created 2026-05-11) and nothing about it should have been
skipped, which pointed at the method rather than the data.

The list pages with ORDER BY sierra_update_date DESC NULLS LAST. That key is not
unique - thousands of rows share a NULL - and SQLite orders ties arbitrarily, so
walking 46k records 5,000 at a time can return a row twice and never return another.
Every bulk audit and repair run that way looked complete and was not.

id_asc gives a unique key to page through. The default sort is unchanged, so the UI
behaves exactly as before. The audits are being re-run against it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Names: an email address in first_name was merging into the greeting
entries.title: Names: an email address in first_name was merging into the greeting
entries.body:
{{first_name}} fell back to "there" only when the column was EMPTY. A column holding
"Drewglenn04@hotmail.com" is not empty, so it merged verbatim:

  Hi Drewglenn04@hotmail.com,

1,136 records hold an email address in first_name, 65 hold a placeholder ("None",
"Unknown", "Owner", "Resident"), and a few hold mojibake from a bad import. AI
enrollment already screened these out (ai-enrollment.js:318) but the drip merge and the
seller SMS opener did not. usableFirstName now degrades all of them to "there" the same
way an empty column already did, and the seller campaign's texts use the same guard.

None of them is in a live campaign today, but the Home Value engine reads the whole
file, so homeValueEligibility now requires a usable first name too.

Data repaired, 1,313 records:
  - Mc/O' capitalisation       Mcmahan -> McMahan          467 + 11
  - ALL CAPS                   MARIUS SHELBY -> Marius Shelby   1
  - full name in first_name    "Tim Healy" -> Tim | Healy       208
  - middle initials dropped    "Katie T" -> Katie, "C Kendall" -> Kendall   253 + 248
  - "And" -> "and"             "Cynthia And Ernie" -> "Cynthia and Ernie"
  - HTML entities decoded      "Jerry & Melissa" -> "Jerry & Melissa"
  - stray and doubled spaces

Left alone on purpose:
  - 102 entities (trusts, estates, LLCs, churches, banks) - never rearranged
  - couples with no surname ("Sydney and Logan"): which word is the surname is a guess
  - "B J", "R J", "W D": a name that IS initials keeps both, because dropping the last
    token would leave "B". Only a middle initial after a real first name is dropped.
  - Mac names (Mackenzie, Mackinaw, Macbride) - spelled that way, and pinned in a test
  - 1,230 junk records with no recoverable name; the guard greets them as "there"

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Addresses: the street suffix was stranded in the city column on 861 records
entries.title: Addresses: the street suffix was stranded in the city column on 861 records
entries.body:
Found by running every stored address through the real render function instead of
pattern-matching the data, which is how the stranded quadrant was missed the first
time. This is the same import bug one word further along:

  "301 N Gill"            city "St"                -> "301 N Gill St"
  "402 N Center"          city "Point Rd Hiawatha"  -> "402 N Center Point Rd", Hiawatha
  "2116 SW 17th"          city "St"                -> "2116 SW 17th St"

usableCity('Dr') returned 'Dr', so those people would have been greeted as living in
"Dr" or "Ct". The guard now rejects a bare street suffix, and the 861 records have the
suffix back on the street.

Only street-TYPE words are in the list. Center, Point, Grove and Springs are
deliberately left out, because they are real town names here - every one of Center
Point, Mount Vernon, Central City, North Liberty and Belle Plaine still passes.

Two cases the first pass got wrong and this one handles: a quadrant is not appended
when the street already carries it ("2825 NW Schultz Drive" + city "NW Quadrant" must
not gain a second NW), and "Quadrant" is a label for a part of town, not the name of
one, so it is not kept as a city.

Where the city value held nothing but the suffix the town is now empty rather than
guessed - 853 of the 861. Seven kept a real town that was sitting behind the suffix.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Addresses: a street named after a town kept its name, plus round-2 format rules
entries.title: Addresses: a street named after a town kept its name, plus round-2 format rules
entries.body:
A wider audit than the case/quadrant pass, prompted by John asking what was still
wrong. Two of these were live bugs, not cosmetics.

TOWN_TAIL was eating part of good streets. It let the zip be zero digits long and,
under the /i flag, "Rd" satisfied the two-letter state slot, so " Alburnett Rd."
looked exactly like a city tail and

  5328 N. Alburnett Rd.  ->  5328 N

John confirmed the record was already correct ("5328 N Alburnett Rd, Central City,
IA 52214") - the data was fine and this function was the thing breaking it. A city
tail is now only recognised when something marks it as one: a zip, the state, or a
comma directly before the town. Every street named Marion, Solon, Vinton, Amana or
Alburnett keeps its name, and the real jammed tails still trim.

Also folded into the unconditional pass beside the quadrant, for the same reason -
these are wrong in any casing, so an all-one-case test cannot be what decides
whether to fix them:
  - Mc/O' capitalisation   Mcgowan -> McGowan   (93 records)
  - unit spacing           Unit#310 -> Unit 310  (5)
  - trailing punctuation    "955 Oak St." -> "955 Oak St"  (30 periods, 436 commas)
  - directional period     "5328 N. Alburnett Rd" -> "5328 N Alburnett Rd"  (3)
  - a city column holding a street line or bare state is not a town  (264)

Data repaired to match: 854 records in round 2, plus 3 directional periods. A sweep
of all 23,679 mailable addresses through the real usableStreet now shows 23,578
rendering exactly as stored, 0 trimmed, and 101 falling back to "your home" - PO
boxes, "None", number-only and name-only values that cannot be repaired without new
data.

Deliberately NOT changed: Mac names (Macbride, Mackenzie, Mackinaw are spelled that
way), and 12 records whose address or city contains a newline, because those are two
values in one field and collapsing the newline would splice two different addresses
into one line.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Merge fields: a quadrant is uppercase, and "Ne" is not a town
entries.title: Merge fields: a quadrant is uppercase, and "Ne" is not a town
entries.body:
A live preview of the first five home-value enrollments caught two things the
all-one-case tidier could not see, because it only touched values that were
entirely one case:

  What could 3025 Towne House Dr Ne be worth today?

"Dr Ne" was already mixed case, so it was left alone. 10,479 records carry a
quadrant written that way. A quadrant is not a word, so tidyCase now uppercases
it whatever the rest of the value looks like, and the case test reads the
original so an all-lowercase address still gets title-cased.

Separately, 782 imported rows had the street's own quadrant sitting alone in the
city column ("600 Nilsen Rd" with city "Ne") - the address split at the wrong
point, which would have greeted someone as living in "Ne". usableCity now
rejects a bare quadrant so the copy falls back to "your area", and
processLead puts the quadrant back on the street and treats the city as
missing. Without that second half the sync's empty-city backfill would keep
restoring it. The town itself is not recoverable for most of these rows - only
118 have a trustworthy zip - so none is invented.

Three older assertions expected the lower-case quadrant to pass through
untouched. They were pinning the bug, and are corrected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Merge fields: stop imported ALL-CAPS addresses shouting from the subject line
entries.title: Merge fields: stop imported ALL-CAPS addresses shouting from the subject line
entries.body:
Checking the campaign's custom fields turned this up: 3,441 addresses and 3,841
cities are stored entirely in capitals, so roughly one recipient in eight would
have received "What could 1117 DEER RUN DRIVE NORTHEAST be worth today?" — which
reads as spam and is the opposite of the tone this campaign wants.

Fully-uppercase values are now title-cased at render. Anything already mixed case
was typed that way by a person and is left untouched. NE/NW/SE/SW stay capitals
because they are not words, and Mc/O' names keep their inner capital.

Also added the three tokens this campaign introduced — street_address,
city_or_area, home_value_url — to the merge-field list. They worked, but were
missing from the picker, so nobody editing a template could see they existed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Marketing email: one send window, 9-5, across every campaign
entries.title: Marketing email: one send window, 9-5, across every campaign
entries.body:
John. The windows had drifted apart -- 9-11, 9-12, 9-14, 9-16, 9-17 and one step
at 9-11:30 -- so identical campaigns behaved differently depending on when they
were built. All 13 now run 09:00-17:00.

A wider window also paces better: the scheduler picks a random minute inside it,
so a 200-lead day lands as a trickle across eight hours rather than a burst before
noon. That matters more now that Home Value can add 200 a day on top of the
existing traffic.

Already-scheduled sends keep their time; this governs what is scheduled from here.
Prior values recorded before the change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value: past clients only via the Lifelong Friends nurture, plus named exclusions
entries.title: Home Value: past clients only via the Lifelong Friends nurture, plus named exclusions
entries.body:
John's rule. A Closed lead qualifies only if already in a Lifelong Friends
past-client nurture. That list was hand-picked to leave out anyone who transacted
recently, so it carries a judgement the Hub cannot make for itself -- nothing in
the data records when somebody last bought or sold. Past clients who were never
put through that selection are left alone and John adds them by hand.

Named exclusions too, for people the team is actively working with: a listing
being prepared, a valuation visit last week. Stored as a setting so more can be
added without a deploy.

The preview now also explains why fewer past clients qualify than sit in the
nurture: membership is one requirement, the address and email rules are the
others, and some fail those.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value preview: show WHY a past client is not in a past-client drip
entries.title: Home Value preview: show WHY a past client is not in a past-client drip
entries.body:
"Not in a past-client drip" and "transacted recently" are not the same thing,
and which of the two those 387 leads actually are decides whether excluding them
is right or just convenient. Splits them into never enrolled, enrolled before but
not active now, and active in some other campaign.

Read-only.

entries.subject: Home Value preview: count over all eligible rows, not the capped sample
entries.title: Home Value preview: count over all eligible rows, not the capped sample
entries.body:
Counting Closed leads from the returned sample understated them: the sample is
capped at 200 and the /activity endpoint it was cross-referenced against returns
at most 500 of 1,034 enrollments. Both numbers looked like findings and were
artefacts. Counts now come from the full set and from drip_enrollments directly.

Read-only.

entries.subject: Home Value: 30-day lookup rule, and a record-only intake to seed it
entries.title: Home Value: 30-day lookup rule, and a record-only intake to seed it
entries.body:
John: do not enroll anyone who checked their value in the last 30 days. Someone
who looked last week should not be asked to look again; someone who looked a year
ago is fair to ask. Replaces the blanket "has the tag" exclusion, which shut out
past lookups forever.

Recency comes from the intake's own log, so it covers submissions the Hub never
saw. Which needs the history seeded -- hence recordOnly: it logs the submission
and tags the lead but sends nothing and defers nothing, so backfilling old
notifications cannot email somebody today about a lookup they did weeks ago.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value: runs alongside other campaigns, 90-day reset, intake off the email
entries.title: Home Value: runs alongside other campaigns, 90-day reset, intake off the email
entries.body:
John, three things.

Campaigns can now overlap where it makes sense. enrollInDrip gains allowConcurrent
so Home Value sits beside Before the Sign rather than being refused, and the rule
that matters -- never two campaign emails to one person in a day -- moved to SEND
time in advanceDrip. It had to: a check at enrollment cannot catch a collision
that happens in week 14. A send that would be the second today is pushed to
tomorrow and logged; the other one keeps its slot.

A submission now defers the campaign 90 days instead of pausing it. The
enrollment stays ACTIVE with a future date, because a paused one needs somebody
to remember to resume it and nobody ever does.

And the intake reads the Sierra notification email rather than waiting for the
tag. It has to: both submissions on 09-28 were in Gmail and in Sierra within
seconds and still had not reached the Hub hours later. One submission finds or
creates the lead, tags it, records the estimates and what they told the form,
sends the Loom follow-up, and starts the 90-day clock. Repeat visits are counted
rather than collapsed -- a second or third look is the strongest signal here.

Parser is pinned against the real notification text. The detail block opens on
the same line as its label, so a line-anchored match silently missed the address;
the tests caught it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value: automatic enrollment, paced, OFF by default
entries.title: Home Value: automatic enrollment, paced, OFF by default
entries.body:
John's rules. Qualifies on a real street address (usableStreet, so a PO box or
"None" does not count), status not active/pending/junk/donotcontact (matched
case-insensitively, because the data holds both "junk" and "Junk"), not an FSBO
or Expired lead, a real non-opted-out email whose status is ValidAddress,
TwoWayEmailing or Unknown, and no prior use of the home value tool -- somebody who
just checked their value should get a conversation, not a drip about checking it.

Paced at 200 a day. The rate is the point: the Hub has sent ~10,000 emails in its
life and this campaign is ~583,000 over six months.

Nobody gets two campaign emails in one day. enrollInDrip already refuses a lead
active in any other drip, which covers it more thoroughly than a date check, and
the same-day guard stays as a second line.

pauseOnHomeValueSubmission stops the drip the moment someone uses the tool, so a
person picks the conversation up from there.

Nothing runs until home_value_enroll_enabled is 1. /home-value/preview shows who
would go next and why the rest would not, and sends nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Inbox: search the team mailboxes by subject, read-only
entries.title: Inbox: search the team mailboxes by subject, read-only
entries.body:
The poller only stores a message it can match to a client, by design, so anything
sent by a system rather than a person never reaches the Hub and cannot be found
there -- a Sierra "Contact Request" from the home value site being the case in
hand. This asks the mailbox directly, over Gmail's All Mail so archived messages
count, and writes nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Email: unsubscribe is just the word; Home Value carries the business address
entries.title: Email: unsubscribe is just the word; Home Value carries the business address
entries.body:
John, both. The footer line is now the linked word "Unsubscribe" on its own,
with no sentence wrapped around it.

And a physical postal address is required on commercial email under CAN-SPAM,
which these are. Added to all 26 Home Value templates. Taken from the team's own
site, which publishes it in both its visible footer and its schema.org
PostalAddress, rather than guessed at from listing data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.title: Test: slice the tracking block to its end, not a guessed character count

The footer markup grew and the fixed 1800-character window stopped reaching the

entries.subject: Email: the unsubscribe line sits inside the card's width, not against the page edge
entries.title: Email: the unsubscribe line sits inside the card's width, not against the page edge
entries.body:
SendGrid appends subscription_tracking AFTER the whole body, so on a designed
email it landed outside the 640px card and would have sat full-width against the
page edge, out of line with everything above it. Centering it in a table of the
same width and padding keeps it reading as the last line of the email.

entries.subject: Email: gate the unsubscribe on marketing mail, not on "has a category"
entries.title: Email: gate the unsubscribe on marketing mail, not on "has a category"
entries.body:
Found while checking whether the change actually covered all marketing email:
it covered far too much. EVERY automated send carries a category, so gating on
one existing would have put an unsubscribe footer on a password reset, a
calendar invite, an internal lead alert and an Inbox 1:1 -- the personal mail I
had said would stay clean.

isBulkCategory names the marketing ones explicitly: drip_<id>, auto_<id>, and
the bulk composer. Everything else is transactional, internal, or one person
writing to one person, and gets nothing.

Tested against the real categories the codebase sends with, password_reset
among them, so a new send path cannot quietly inherit a footer it should not
have.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Email: bulk mail carries an unsubscribe again, 1:1 mail does not
entries.title: Email: bulk mail carries an unsubscribe again, 1:1 mail does not
entries.body:
John's reading matches what the account settings showed: Marketing Campaigns
manages unsubscribes itself, the Email API does not, and the Hub uses the Email
API. The account's own Subscription Tracking is off and there are no ASM groups,
so nothing the Hub has ever sent carried an opt-out link -- the new campaign and
every existing drip alike.

So subscription tracking is set per send, and only when a category is present:
drips, sequences and campaigns carry it, while a 1:1 email an agent types to one
person stays clean.

html and text are supplied rather than a substitution_tag. A tag is only swapped
where a template already contains it, and none of the 375 templates does -- that
is precisely how the missing link went unnoticed the first time round.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Drips: send the next step now instead of waiting for its slot
entries.title: Drips: send the next step now instead of waiting for its slot
entries.body:
Somebody enrolls a lead and wants the first email to go today rather than
tomorrow morning. /delay could only push a send later; there was no way to bring
one forward.

Runs the real advanceDrip, so the enrollment moves on exactly as if the scheduler
had picked it up -- the step advances, the next one is scheduled, the send is
logged -- and every guard still applies: junk/DNC pulls them out, a reply pauses
the campaign. It ignores the step's send-time window on purpose, since asking for
it now is the intent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Email diagnostic: match SendGrid's real setting names
entries.title: Email diagnostic: match SendGrid's real setting names
entries.body:
SendGrid calls them "click", "open" and "subscription", not "*_tracking".
Matching the longer name returned null for all three, which read as "nothing is
configured" when it only meant "nothing matched". Also lists every setting name
and its enabled flag, so a future rename cannot quietly produce the same wrong
answer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Email: read-only view of what SendGrid's account does to our mail
entries.title: Email: read-only view of what SendGrid's account does to our mail
entries.body:
Working out why drip emails carry no unsubscribe link. The Hub's 375 templates
contain no unsubscribe and no SendGrid substitution tag, and the saved signature
has none either -- so if anything is being added, the account is adding it, and
guessing was not going to settle it.

Returns subscription tracking, the account footer, ASM groups and whether the
suppression list is reachable. Settings and group names only, never the key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Email: the logo travels with the message instead of loading on open
entries.title: Email: the logo travels with the message instead of loading on open
entries.body: John: the logo takes a second or two to appear. It was a hosted , so it is only requested when the reader opens the message. Now it is an inline (cid:) attachment that rides along inside the email, so it is already there the moment the email renders. Nothing to fetch, nothing to wait for, and no dependency on the Hub being reachable at the moment somebody opens a six-month-old email. Templates still store the hosted URL, which keeps the Hub's own template preview working; the swap happens at send time. Also fixed the weight while I was in there. The header shows the logo at 210px and the file was 800px wide, so roughly four times the pixels were downloaded and thrown away. public/email-logo.jpg is the same artwork at 2x its display size: 14KB against 44KB, 67% smaller. Callers can now set an attachment's disposition and content_id; the default is still 'attachment', so nothing that sends files changes behaviour. Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context)

entries.subject: Drips: send one step to an address, to check a campaign before it goes live
entries.title: Drips: send one step to an address, to check a campaign before it goes live
entries.body:
Testing through the composer route would have been misleading: /api/email/send
appends the saved signature to whatever it is handed, and a drip send never does,
so the test email would carry a signature block the real one does not have.

This goes through sendSequenceEmail, the same path the campaign uses, and renders
merge fields against a real lead so the address and city handling is actually
exercised. It sends to the address asked for rather than the lead's own, so any
lead can be the merge source without mailing them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Merge fields: an address that is not a street line falls back instead of sending
entries.title: Merge fields: an address that is not a street line falls back instead of sending
entries.body:
John, for the records the cleanup could not repair. An address merge field is not
like a name: it lands in a SUBJECT LINE, so a bad record reads as nonsense rather
than as a blank. "What could Po Box 165 be worth today?" and "What could None be
worth today?" were both real, waiting to be sent.

The ~126 addresses and ~106 cities left after the data pass cannot be fixed by any
transform -- a PO box, "None", a bare house number, a street sitting in the city
column. So they are handled at render instead of in the data: anything that does
not read like a street line becomes "your home", anything that does not read like
a town becomes "your area". The copy was already written for both, so those
records still send a sentence that makes sense rather than being skipped.

It also repairs on the fly, so a row that arrives dirty tomorrow needs no cleanup
run: a jammed "180 Rosedale Road Marion IA 52302" is trimmed to the street before
use. Trimming is anchored on the town names, not the state, because cutting at the
state turns that same address into "180" -- it eats the street.

Tests use the real broken values from the audit, including the false alarms that
must survive untouched: "3300 Iowa Ave SE" and "2449 Wisconsin St Sw" are real
addresses that merely use a state name as a street name.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value Weekly: footer drops the "database" line, carries real contact details
entries.title: Home Value Weekly: footer drops the "database" line, carries real contact details
entries.body:
John: nobody should be told they are in a database and being watched. Out go
"You are receiving this because you are a homeowner in our database" and the
"Cedar Rapids & Marion, Iowa" line. The disclaimer stays, because an automated
estimate really is a starting point and not an appraisal.

In its place the footer now carries who to actually contact: Matt, the team and
brokerage, phone, email and site. No separate signature block -- the footer IS
the signature for these.

Also gave the logo an explicit height. Several clients, Outlook among them,
reserve no space for an image without one, which is the difference between a
logo appearing and a broken-image box sitting there while images load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value Weekly: drop the in-body unsubscribe, leave SendGrid's own in charge
entries.title: Home Value Weekly: drop the in-body unsubscribe, leave SendGrid's own in charge
entries.body:
John: the SendGrid account already appends an unsubscribe on send, so the emails
should not carry their own.

Reverting the per-send subscription_tracking I added with it, because it was the
more dangerous half. Setting it per-send OVERRIDES the account-level default, so
once the {{unsubscribe}} token left the body that override would have inserted
nothing and quietly removed the opt-out link altogether -- worse than the gap I
thought I was closing. Unset, SendGrid's own footer stays in charge.

Also recorded in the builder that the value site asks for the address every time
by design: Sierra exposes no way to prefill it (six parameter spellings tested,
the field stays empty), and that is accepted rather than a limitation to solve.

All 26 rebuilt and re-verified: no unsubscribe text left in any body, and all
26 CTAs resolve to the team value site.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value Weekly: week 3 subject uses the area, not the address
entries.title: Home Value Weekly: week 3 subject uses the area, not the address
entries.body:
{{street_address}} there degraded to "homes around your home" for a lead with
no address on file. The email is about the area anyway, so the area token reads
right both ways: "around Marion" / "around your area".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Home Value Weekly: 26-email homeowner campaign, plus an opt-out for bulk mail
entries.title: Home Value Weekly: 26-email homeowner campaign, plus an opt-out for bulk mail
entries.body:
A 6-month weekly homeowner drip built as data + one shell rather than 26 hand-written
emails, so subjects, copy, CTA labels, order and timing stay editable: the 26 land as
ordinary Hub templates and the schedule as an ordinary drip, both editable in the UI.
scripts/home-value-weekly.mjs rebuilds them in place by name and never duplicates.

Three merge tokens the campaign needed:
  {{street_address}}  alias of address, so homeowner copy reads as what it is
  {{city_or_area}}    {{city}} falls back to "Cedar Rapids", which asserts where
                      someone lives; this one degrades to "your area" instead
  {{home_value_url}}  the bare URL, for a designed email that puts the value tool
                      behind its own button and needs the href, not a sentence

And a compliance fix found on the way in: sequence/drip mail went out with NO
unsubscribe link at all. SendGrid subscription tracking is now enabled for any send
carrying a category -- drips, sequences, campaigns -- and never for a 1:1 email an
agent types to one person. The Event Webhook already turns an `unsubscribe` event into
the marketing opt-out flag, so the loop closes itself.

Copy is evergreen throughout. Nothing claims a value moved, a neighbour sold, or an
equity or mortgage figure, because the Hub holds no per-property valuation feed to
support such a claim. The builder audits before it writes: banned money/urgency wording
in subjects, subject length, body word count, 26 distinct subjects, CTA-label variety.

Nobody is enrolled. Starting it is a separate, deliberate step.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Backfill a matched lead's blank phone from the master file sync
entries.title: Backfill a matched lead's blank phone from the master file sync
entries.body:
A lead created before the sheet row had a phone (a timing race between the
daily MLS pull and the Forewarn lookup) never got one, because no later sync
revisited it once phone became Hub-owned data. Fill it once, when still blank;
never overwrite a phone that's already there.

entries.subject: Profile: picture sits beside the social links, not at the column edge
entries.title: Profile: picture sits beside the social links, not at the column edge
entries.body:

entries.subject: Search: find a lead by phone in any format, alternate numbers included
entries.title: Search: find a lead by phone in any format, alternate numbers included
entries.body:
Numbers are stored formatted -- "(319) 551-6347" for 4,470 of 4,471 leads -- and
both search clauses compared that text literally. So the forms people actually
use returned nothing and the lead looked like it did not exist: a pasted
"3195516347", a "319-551-6347", a "+13195516347" off a caller ID. Only the exact
stored string or a fragment of it worked. Alternate numbers were never searched
at all, on either bar.

Now both sides are reduced to digits before comparing. SQLite has no regex, so
the stored value is stripped with nested REPLACE() of the punctuation phone
numbers carry. 11+ typed digits keep the last 10, so a country code still
matches a locally-stored number.

Two deliberate limits. Commas are NOT stripped: alt_phones is a comma-separated
list, and keeping the separator stops one number's tail running into the next
one's head. And under 7 digits is not treated as a phone -- a street number, a
ZIP or a year would otherwise add noise to a name or address search.

Shared by the Clients list and the global search bar so the two cannot drift.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Before the Sign: drop "Sell as-is, or fix it first?" (step 4 of 30)
entries.title: Before the Sign: drop "Sell as-is, or fix it first?" (step 4 of 30)
entries.body:
It was driving unsubscribes, so John asked for it out of the seller nurture
sequence.

Removing it is not just a splice. Drip steps are a positional array, and BOTH
the enrollment pointer (current_step) and the send-dedupe key
(drip{id}_step{idx}) are that index. Splicing one out mid-sequence slides every
later step down onto a key that already reads "sent", so the runner would find
a prior success, skip the send and advance -- silently burning through the rest
of the campaign for the 452 active leads past that point.

So the migration drops the step, discards its own execution rows, then slides
each later index and its key down by one, ascending so the UNIQUE key never
collides, and decrements current_step for everyone past it. Leads before it
simply never receive it; leads already past it keep every remaining email.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

and the step never advanced: 5 min later the row was still due, the 60-min
dedup deferred it +3h, and Luis received the identical opener 8 times over
3 days (3x/day inside the 9-4 automation window).

Fixes: correct params via extracted advanceSellerStep (exported, tested);
sendSellerSms wrapped in try/catch like the FSBO sender; each sweep row is
failure-isolated (error -> +3h push + activity_log, never a hot loop); and
a self-heal guard — an identical already-sent body advances the step
instead of ever re-texting. Luis's row set to stopped (human decision on
any further contact).

entries.subject: Design Upgrade Phase 1: toasts replace all 293 alerts, promise confirms replace all 63 confirms, first-load skeletons
entries.title: Design Upgrade Phase 1: toasts replace all 293 alerts, promise confirms replace all 63 confirms, first-load skeletons
entries.body:
Per HUB-DESIGN-UPGRADE-PLAN.md Phase 1 (guided by ask-sonner + emil-design-eng
+ impeccable):

1.1 Sonner Toaster mounted once at the root — theme-aware (follows the Hub's
    light/dark), bottom-right desktop / top-center mobile, styled with our
    tokens, above every modal. Every alert() (293 across 25 files) now routes
    through notify(), which classifies legacy messages into success / error /
    neutral toasts so saves stop blocking the UI and errors carry their reason.

1.2 confirmDialog() replaces every native confirm() (63 sites): promise-based
    dialog on our tokens — title states the action, body the consequence,
    destructive button red and right-aligned, Cancel focused by default,
    Escape cancels, Enter never confirms. Legacy multi-line messages split
    into title + body automatically. 9 handlers async-ified (build-verified).
    Native confirm() in the installed PWA broke the app illusion completely.

1.3 First-load skeletons on the two highest-traffic lists (Clients, Inbox)
    using the existing shimmer tokens — first paint only; refreshes and the
    10-min sync updates keep rendering in place, never blanking data.

entries.subject: Fix the real root causes of the all-day page crashes: stale/poisoned PWA cache + Dashboard hooks bug
entries.title: the real root causes of the all-day page crashes: stale/poisoned PWA cache + Dashboard hooks bug
entries.body:
Four layers, found while triple-checking:

1. Dashboard React #310: two useState hooks (master-sync button) sat BELOW the
   loading early-returns, so the first data render had more hooks than the
   loading render — crashed every Dashboard open without cached data. Hooks
   moved above the returns.
2. Server SPA fallback served index.html for MISSING /assets chunks (old builds
   after a deploy) with HTTP 200 — now a 404, never HTML under a .js URL.
3. Service worker v8: purges the caches those HTML responses poisoned (fixes
   every affected device automatically on next visit), and only caches asset
   responses whose content-type matches the URL.
4. Self-healing tabs: hourly update check, one-shot reload when a new service
   worker takes over, one-shot reload when a lazy chunk fails to load
   (vite:preloadError), and the crash screen's "Try again" now does a real
   reload instead of re-rendering the same broken code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

model: no eligible FSBO reaches 14 days on market and gets forgotten.

every send, profile card, preview and smart lists. Trigger = LIVE listing DOM >= 14
from the master sync (imported above threshold qualifies immediately; DOM < 14 is

line screen, cached verdict), prior meaningful seller response (shared

duplicate phone, durable manual removal. Deferrals: recent human contact, pending
manual text. Approved opening copy unchanged (Steps 1-3), then ~weekly 6-8d-jitter
rotation from a low-pressure DOM-gated angle bank; "the home at {address}", never

Response task, notification) then the approved scripted ack + email ask still run.

entries.subject: AI Auto-Enrollment Engine: fresh-lead speed-to-lead + database reactivation (ships OFF)
entries.title: AI Auto-Enrollment Engine: fresh-lead speed-to-lead + database reactivation (ships OFF)
entries.body:
One central evaluator (evaluateAiEnrollmentEligibility) over the Status=New pool
(New is a status, not an age — age never excludes). Three decisions
(eligible/deferred/excluded) with reason codes; four classifications
(fresh / cold never-connected / cold previously-connected / re-engaged dormant);
two lanes: fresh = event hooks + 10-min sweep, immediate + uncapped;
reactivation = hourly weekday-window batches, daily cap (150), priority-ordered,
2-3 min staggered first sends. Hard exclusions always win: prospecting source
origins (exact source-field match from the audited production distribution;
migration != origin), FSBO/MLS identity, CX Connect fence, STOP/DNT/undeliverable,
autopilot tag excludes, active transactions, durable manual exclusion, already
AI-managed. Enrollment != sending — full policy stack still gates every send.

Deduped audit log (ai_enrollment_log) + ai_lead_state exclusion columns;
/api/ai/enrollment/* routes incl. zero-write dry-run preview; Settings card with
modes Manual / Fresh only / Fresh + Reactivation; smart lists (candidates,
enrolled today); profile decision line + exclude button; 23-test suite
(230/230 green; CX dry-run test de-flaked to per-lead counts).

entries.subject: Email engagement tracking: SendGrid Event Webhook end to end
entries.title: Email engagement tracking: SendGrid Event Webhook end to end
entries.body:
Sends now request open+click tracking. New public POST /api/email/events (ECDSA
signature verification when the webhook public key is configured) matches events
to the exact email via sg_message_id prefix = email_log.provider_message_id (+
recipient for multi-row sends). Idempotent by construction: raw events dedupe on
UNIQUE sg_event_id and all summaries are recomputed from raw rows (MIN/MAX/COUNT)
so retries/out-of-order arrivals never double-count. Adds email_events table,
email_log summary fields (delivered/first/last opened+clicked, counts, last URL,
delivery_status), and indexed client rollups (last_email_opened_at etc.). Surfaces:
Clients columns Last Email Opened/Clicked + Opens/Clicks with server-side sort,
opened/clicked filters (ever/never/N days, min counts), smart lists Opened Email
(7d) + Clicked-No Reply, Inbox engagement chips, profile email cards with an
expandable event timeline, Reporting aggregates endpoint, spamreport/unsubscribe
-> marketing_email_opt_out, and opens/clicks feed the AI behavioral score at the
pre-existing weights (open 1, click 3). Pre-webhook emails show No tracking data,
never 'never opened'. Setup endpoint POST /api/email/setup-events-webhook.

entries.subject: AI suggestions: analyze the whole thread, never treat a stale reply as fresh
entries.title: AI suggestions: analyze the whole thread, never treat a stale reply as fresh

was months old and WE had already answered it and followed up since, so drafts
re-answered old messages (e.g. re-replying to a June text in September). Now:
context carries lastDirection + latestInboundAt; when the thread ends with OUR
messages, buildUserMessage and the inbox suggest path state the real SITUATION
(their last message was N days ago, we've messaged since, analyze the entire
conversation including our follow-ups, never repeat or re-answer). The Continue-

different anchor when their last line was already answered. Prompt version bumped.

entries.subject: Fix natural-language opt-out false positives (e.g. 'I dont check my text messages')
entries.title: natural-language opt-out false positives (e.g. 'I dont check my text messages')
entries.body:
The NL_OPTOUT_RE 24-char window matched benign phrases where an opt-out verb sat
near a messaging NOUN with an intervening reading verb or possessive -- 'I dont
check my text messages', 'I dont always answer texts' -- and wrongly set
hub_text_opt_out, blocking texts to engaged leads (e.g. Tammy Facion, an active
FSBO sharing a door code). Tightened the regex with two negative lookaheads (no
following check/read/answer/etc verb; no possessive + messaging noun) so it still
catches real opt-outs ('stop texting me', 'dont text me', 'no more texts', 'take
me off') but not these. Added POST /api/inbox/fix-false-optouts (?dry=1) to clear
existing NL false-positive opt-outs (source sms_reply_nl only; literal STOP kept).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: AI: apply FSBO/expired/cancelled cold-seller conversation philosophy
entries.title: AI: apply FSBO/expired/cancelled cold-seller conversation philosophy
entries.body:
These leads did not ask us to contact them, so they must not be handled like a
normal inbound seller. Added a COLD_SELLER_PHILOSOPHY block + detectColdSeller()
(reads fsbo_status/mls_status, falls back to tags/source) that OVERRIDES the
discovery ladder, objection playbook and appointment cadence: listen -> understand
-> acknowledge -> help -> stay available, relationship over pitch, no interrogation,
soft curiosity, mirror energy, never challenge/bad-mouth prior agent/assume price,
never fake value, no sales cliches, mention Matt/walkthrough only when it naturally
fits. Wired into BOTH prompt systems (autopilot buildSystemPrompt + inbox suggested
replies generateReply) and the sandbox. Added 5 regression scenarios + made the
eval scorer accept an array of acceptable actions. Bumped AI_PROMPT_VERSION.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Inbox: stop group replies being duplicated as 1:1 texts (Twilio dual-webhook)
entries.title: Inbox: stop group replies being duplicated as 1:1 texts (Twilio dual-webhook)
entries.body:
A Twilio Conversations (group) participant's reply arrives on the group webhook
(conv_<IM sid>) AND, in this number config, the plain messaging webhook fires for
the same SMS (twilio_<SM sid>) — different MessageSids, so external_id dedup missed.
That created a second copy on the person's profile and a stray standalone 1:1
conversation. Now the messaging webhook skips any sender that's a known group
participant (isGroupParticipant), the group webhook sends the inbound notification
(no AI auto-reply into groups), and a maintenance endpoint /dedupe-group-mirrors
cleans up the historical duplicates.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
